children.translated_text: <s>Guḍūcī</s> is also called <s>amṛtavallī</s>, <s>chinnā</s>, <s>chinnaruhā</s>, and <s>amṛtā</s>;
it is remembered as <s>chinnodbhavā</s>, <s>amṛtalatā</s>, <s>dhārā</s>, and <s>vatsādanī</s>.
That same plant is also called <s>somavallī</s>, <s>kuṇḍalī</s>, and <s>cakralakṣaṇā</s>;
it is said to be <s>nāgakumārī</s>, <s>chinnāṅgī</s>, and destroyer of fever.
It is <s>jīvantī</s>, <s>madhuparṇī</s>, <s>tantrikā</s>, and <s>devanirmitā</s>;
it is <s>vayaḥsthā</s>, <s>maṇḍalī</s>, gentle <s>saumyā</s>, <s>viśalyā</s>, and born of nectar.
It is rejuvenating, earthy, moon-bright, and victorious for physicians;
another kind is bulb-born: <s>kandā</s>, <s>amṛtakandā</s>, and <s>guḍūcikā</s>.
It is <s>piṇḍāmṛtā</s>, much-cut, and is also called <s>kandarohiṇī</s>.
In its fresh juice <s>guḍūcī</s> is bitter, astringent, hot, and also heavy;
it is supreme for removing disorders from the three doṣas, worms, blood diseases, piles, skin disease, and fever.
<s>Guḍūcī</s> grants long life, benefits the intellect, is bitter, constipating, and strengthening;
it conquers fever, thirst, anemia, vāta disorders, blood disorders, vomiting, urinary disease, and the three doṣas.
<s>Guḍūcī</s> removes kapha and vāta and dries up pitta and fat;
it pacifies blood and vāta and destroys itching and erysipelas.
The bulb-born <s>guḍūcī</s> is pungent and hot and removes the combined doṣic disorder <s>saṃnipāta</s>;
it counteracts poison, destroys fever and demonic afflictions, and removes wrinkles and gray hair.

children.text: ativiṣā śuklakandā jñeyā viśvā ca bhaṅgurā
children.translated_text: <s>Ativiṣā</s> is known as <s>śuklakandā</s>, <s>viśvā</s>, and <s>bhaṅgurā</s>;
it is <s>śyāmakandā</s>, <s>prativiṣā</s>, <s>śṛṅgī</s>, <s>upaviṣā</s>, and <s>viṣā</s>.

children.text: ārdrā śvetā virūpā ca viṣadā pittavallabhā
children.translated_text: It is moist, white, misshapen, poison-giving, and dear to pitta;
it is <s>ghuṇapriyā</s>, removes diarrhea, and destroys the diseases of children.
<s>Ativiṣā</s> is pungent, hot, and bitter, and removes kapha, pitta, and fever;
it removes diarrhea from indigestion, cough, poison, and vomiting.
<s>Mūrvā</s> has sweet sap and is called <s>devī</s>, <s>pṛthakparṇī</s>, and also <s>triparṇī</s>;
it is <s>devaśreṇī</s>, sweet-sapped, smooth-leaved, and <s>moraṭā</s>.
<s>Mūrvā</s> is sweet in sap and hot, and conquers heart disease, kapha, and vāta;
it destroys skin disease, itching, vomiting, urinary disease, poison, and intermittent fever.
<s>Moraṭa</s> is <s>kīrṇapuṣpa</s>, <s>pīlupuṣpa</s>, and <s>madhusrava</s>;
it is <s>tejanī</s>, long-rooted, <s>puruṣa</s>, and <s>kṣīramoraṭa</s>.
It removes fever and destroys bad taste in the mouth, thirst, and burning;
this <s>kṣīramoraṭa</s> should be known as removing kapha and pitta.
<s>Mañjiṣṭhā</s> is <s>kālameṣī</s>, <s>samaṅgā</s>, and <s>vikasāruṇā</s>;
it is <s>mañjukā</s>, <s>raktayaṣṭī</s>, <s>bhāṇḍī</s>, and also <s>yojanavallī</s>.
It is <s>kṣetriṇī</s>, <s>vijayā</s>, red <s>raktā</s>, red-limbed, and an ornament of cloth;

children.text: jiṅgī bhaṇḍī tathā kālā gaṇḍālī kālameṣikā ||
children.translated_text: it is <s>jiṅgī</s>, <s>bhaṇḍī</s>, <s>kālā</s>, <s>gaṇḍālī</s>, and <s>kālameṣikā</s>.
<s>Mañjiṣṭhā</s> is sweet in taste, astringent, hot, and also heavy;
it conquers severe kapha, wounds, urinary disease, blood disorders, poison, and eye diseases.
<s>Dhanvayāsa</s> is <s>durālambhā</s>, copper-rooted, and <s>kacchurā</s>;
it is <s>durālabhā</s>, hard to touch, <s>yāsa</s>, and <s>dhanvayavāsaka</s>.
<s>Durālambhā</s> is sweet, cold, bitter, and destroys burning;
it destroys intermittent fever, thirst, vomiting, urinary disease, and bewilderment.
<s>Yāsa</s>, <s>yavāsaka</s>, and <s>ananta</s> are <s>bālapattrā</s> and <s>adhikaṇṭaka</s>;
it is far-rooted, sea-ended, long-rooted, and born in the desert.
<s>Yavāsaka</s> is sweet and bitter and removes fever, thirst, and bleeding disorders.

children.text: vāsakaḥ siṃhaparṇī ca vṛṣo vāsātha siṃhikā
children.translated_text: <s>Vāsaka</s> is <s>siṃhaparṇī</s>, <s>vṛṣa</s>, <s>vāsā</s>, and <s>siṃhikā</s>;
it is <s>āṭarūṣa</s>, lion-faced, physician's mother, and <s>āṭarūṣaka</s>.
<s>Āṭarūṣa</s> is cold and bitter, and conquers pitta, phlegm, blood disorders, and cough;
it removes wasting disease, heart disease, vomiting, skin disease, fever, and thirst.
<s>Khadira</s> is red-hearted, <s>gāyatrī</s>, and a tooth-cleaning wood;
it is thorny, tender-leaved, crooked-thorned, and tolerant of injury.
<s>Khadira</s> is bitter in taste, cold, and removes pitta, kapha, and blood disorders;
it is remembered as removing skin disease, indigestion, cough, blood disorders, itching, worms, and morbid doṣas.
Another <s>khadira</s> has white heartwood: <s>somavalka</s> and <s>pathidruma</s>;
it is dark-hearted, <s>nemivṛkṣa</s>, <s>kārmuka</s>, and crooked-thorned.
The white <s>khadira</s> is bitter and cold, and removes pitta and kapha;
it removes disorders of the blood and destroys itching and skin disease.
<s>Nimba</s> is <s>niyamana</s>, <s>netā</s>, <s>picumanda</s>, and very bitter;
it is <s>ariṣṭa</s>, <s>sarvatobhadra</s>, <s>prabhadra</s>, and <s>pāribhadraka</s>.
<s>Nimba</s> has bitter taste, is cold and light, and removes phlegm, blood disorders, and pitta;
used regularly as paste, food, and the like, it destroys skin disease, itching, and wounds.
It ripens an unripe swelling and cleanses a wound once it has ripened.
<s>Mahānimba</s> is remembered as <s>drekī</s>, <s>kārmuka</s>, and <s>viṣamuṣṭika</s>;
it is <s>keśamuṣṭi</s>, best among nimbas, <s>ramyaka</s>, and <s>akṣība</s>.
It is <s>kaiḍarya</s>, <s>picumanda</s>, <s>nimba</s>, <s>ariṣṭa</s>, and excellent-barked;
it stops vomiting, has asafoetida-like resin, and is <s>priyaśāla</s> and mountain-born.
<s>Mahānimba</s> is bitter in taste, cold, and removes pitta and kapha;
it destroys skin disease and blood disorders, and when used regularly it checks cholera-like <s>visūcī</s>.
<s>Kirātatiktaka</s> is <s>haima</s>, stem-bitter, and <s>kirātaka</s>;
it is <s>bhūnimba</s>, excessively bitter, <s>kirāta</s>, and <s>rāmasenaka</s>.
Another variety is called <s>nepāla</s>, an ender of fever;
it is very bitter, bitter, enemy of sleep, and remover of <s>saṃnipāta</s>.
<s>Kirātaka</s> is bitter in taste, neither hot nor cold, and also light;
it removes phlegm, pitta, blood disorders, swelling, pain, cough, thirst, and fever.
<s>Kaṭukā</s> is <s>matsyaśakalā</s>, <s>matsyapittā</s>, and <s>rohiṇī</s>;
it is black-variegated, stem-growing, and by name <s>kaṭukarohiṇī</s>.
It is <s>aśokarohiṇī</s>, bitter, wheel-marked, and <s>śakulādanī</s>;
<s>Kaṭurohiṇī</s>, <s>ariṣṭā</s>, and <s>tiktakarohiṇī</s> are also stated.

children.text: āmaghnī śataparvā ca viprāṅgī jananī janā
children.translated_text: It is <s>āmaghnī</s>, hundred-jointed, <s>viprāṅgī</s>, <s>jananī</s>, and <s>janā</s>.
<s>Kaṭukā</s> conquers pitta, is bitter and pungent, cold, and conquers blood disorders and burning;
it destroys phlegmatic weakness and loss of appetite, and removes intermittent fever.
<s>Mustā</s> is <s>ambudhara</s>, <s>megha</s>, <s>ghana</s>, and <s>rājakaseruka</s>.
<s>Bhadramusta</s>, <s>Varaha</s>, <s>Abda</s>, <s>Gangeya</s>, and <s>Kuruvindaka</s> are names.
Then there are <s>Jimuta</s>, <s>Vrsadhvanksi</s>, <s>Jalada</s>, and <s>Balahaka</s>.
Another is called <s>Nadeya</s>, <s>Pindamusta</s>, and <s>Nagara</s>.
<s>Musta</s> is bitter and astringent in taste, very cooling, and conquers phlegm and blood disorders.
It removes bilious fever and diarrhea, and destroys thirst and worms.
<s>Jalamusta</s>, <s>Dasapura</s>, <s>Vaneya</s>, and <s>Paripelava</s>,
<s>Kaivartamusta</s>, <s>Saivala</s>, <s>Jalaja</s>, and <s>Sukahvaya</s> are its names.
The water-born drug is bitter, pungent, astringent, complexion-giving, and cooling.
It promotes intelligence and removes wind disorders, blindness, erysipelas, itching, skin disease, and poison.
<s>Parpata</s> may be called <s>Parpataka</s>, <s>Varatikta</s>, and <s>Sutiktaka</s>.
It is also <s>Rajas</s>, <s>Renu</s>, <s>Pamsu</s>, <s>Kavaca</s>, and <s>Varmakantaka</s>.
<s>Parpata</s> is cooling and bitter, and removes fever arising from pitta and phlegm.
It destroys blood disorders, burning, loss of appetite, exhaustion, intoxication, and dizziness.

children.text: bālakaṃ vāri toyaṃ ca hrīveraṃ jalamambu ca
children.translated_text: <s>Balaka</s>, <s>Vari</s>, <s>Toya</s>, <s>Hrīvera</s>, <s>Jala</s>, and <s>Ambu</s>,
also <s>Kesya</s>, <s>Vajra</s>, <s>Udīcya</s>, <s>Pingama</s>, <s>Acamana</s>, and <s>Kaca</s>, are its names.
<s>Balaka</s> is cooling and bitter, and overcomes pitta, phlegm, and erysipelas.
It removes fever, skin disease, and diarrhea; it benefits the hair and dispels leucoderma and wounds.
<s>Patola</s> is said to be <s>Kulaka</s>, <s>Panduka</s>, and <s>Karkasacchada</s>.
It is <s>Rajiphala</s>, <s>Panduphala</s>, <s>Rajanama</s>, and <s>Amrtaphala</s>.
It is <s>Viryagarbhapratana</s>; it removes skin disease and releases one from cough.
<s>Patola</s> is pungent, bitter, hot, and opposed to pitta.
It destroys phlegm, blood disorders, itching, skin diseases, fever, and burning.
There is another second kind called <s>Patoli</s>; it has sweet leaves and fruit.
The best physician should apply it with the synonyms of <s>Patola</s>.
The leaf of <s>Patola</s> removes pitta, while its vine removes phlegm.
Its fruit pacifies the three doṣas, and its root is purgative.

children.text: haridrā pītikā piṅgā rajanī rañjinī niśā
children.translated_text: <s>Haridra</s> is <s>Pitika</s>, <s>Pinga</s>, <s>Rajani</s>, <s>Ranjini</s>, and <s>Nisa</s>.
It is <s>Gauri</s>, <s>Varnavati</s>, <s>Pita</s>, <s>Harita</s>, and <s>Varavarnini</s>.
<s>Haladika</s>, <s>Bhadralata</s>, and <s>Varnavilasini</s> are to be known as its names.

children.text: viṣaghnī ca jayantī ca dīrgharaṅgā tu raṅgiṇī ||
children.translated_text: It is also <s>Visaghni</s> and <s>Jayanti</s>; because of its lasting color it is <s>Rangini</s>.
<s>Haridra</s> has bitter juice, is dry and hot, and removes poison and urinary disease.
It destroys itching, skin diseases, and wounds, and produces good bodily complexion.
It is purifying, removes worms, and destroys nasal catarrh and loss of appetite.
Another is <s>Daruharidra</s>, also <s>Pitadru</s> and <s>Pitacandana</s>.

children.text: nirdiṣṭā kāṣṭharajanī sā ca kāleyakā smṛtā
children.translated_text: It is designated <s>Kastharajani</s>, and it is remembered as <s>Kaleyaka</s>.
<s>Kaliyaka</s>, <s>Darunisa</s>, <s>Darvi</s>, <s>Pitahva</s>, and <s>Pitaka</s> are its names.
It is <s>Katamkateri</s>, <s>Parjanya</s>, <s>Pitadaru</s>, and <s>Pacampaca</s>.
It is <s>Hemavarnavati</s>, <s>Pita</s>, <s>Hemakanta</s>, and <s>Kusumbhaka</s>.
<s>Daruharidra</s> is bitter, dry, and hot, and conquers wounds and urinary disease.
It destroys pain arising in the ears, eyes, and mouth, and also itching.

children.text: śaṭī śaṭhī palāśā ca jñeyā pṛthupalāśikā
children.translated_text: <s>Sati</s> and <s>Sathi</s> are also <s>Palasa</s>; it should be known as <s>Prthupalasika</s>.
It is <s>Sugandhamula</s>, <s>Gandhali</s>, <s>Sadgrantha</s>, <s>Suvrata</s>, and <s>Vadhu</s>.
It is named <s>Candrani</s>, <s>Candragandha</s>, and <s>Durvidheya</s>.
<s>Sati</s> is bitter, sharp, and hot, and removes fever caused by the combined doṣas.
It removes phlegm, severe wounds, and cough, and brings about purification of the mouth.
Another is <s>Gandhapalasi</s>, also <s>Sthulaka</s> and <s>Tiktakandaka</s>.
It is <s>Tapasi</s> and <s>Jvalani</s>, with leaves and tuber like turmeric.
It removes cough and dyspnea, and dispels hiccup, fever, colic, and wind.
<s>Sati</s> benefits the voice, has fragrant root, is astringent and pungent, and is fluid-promoting.
<s>Mula</s>, <s>Puskaramula</s>, <s>Pauskara</s>, and <s>Puskarahvaya</s>,
<s>Kasmira</s>, <s>Puskarajata</s>, <s>Dhira</s>, and <s>Padmapattraka</s> are its names.
<s>Puskaramula</s> is bitter, pungent, and hot, and conquers phlegm and wind.
It removes fever, anorexia, and cough, and destroys swelling and abdominal distension.

children.text: śvāsaṃ hikkāṃ jayatyeva sevyamānaṃ śanaiḥ śanaiḥ
children.translated_text: When used gradually, it indeed overcomes dyspnea and hiccup.
<s>Bharngi</s>, <s>Gardabhasaka</s>, <s>Padma</s>, and <s>Brahmanayastika</s>,
<s>Angaravalli</s> and <s>Phanji</s> are its names; it is also <s>Brahmasuvarcala</s>.

children.text: śakramātā ca kāsaghnī bhṛṅgajā bhārgavā matā
children.translated_text: It is considered <s>Sakramata</s>, <s>Kasaghni</s>, <s>Bhrngaja</s>, and <s>Bhargava</s>.
<s>Bharngi</s> is bitter in taste, hot, and removes dyspnea and phlegm.
It removes abdominal tumors, fever, blood disorders, and wind; it destroys consumption and nasal catarrh.
<s>Patha</s> is <s>Ambastha</s>, <s>Ambasthaki</s>, <s>Pracina</s>, and <s>Papacelika</s>.
It is <s>Varatikta</s>, <s>Brhattikta</s>, <s>Pathika</s>, <s>Sthapani</s>, and <s>Vrki</s>.

children.text: mālatī ca varā devī trivṛtānyā śubhā matā
children.translated_text: It is also <s>Malati</s>, <s>Vara</s>, <s>Devi</s>, <s>Trivrta</s>, and is regarded as <s>Subha</s>.
<s>Patha</s> has a bitter taste, is aphrodisiac, removes poison, and dispels skin disease and itching.
It overcomes vomiting, heart disease, and fever; it is an excellent pacifier of the three doṣas.
<s>Patha</s> removes diarrhea and colic, and dispels fever from phlegm and pitta.
<s>Svasari</s>, <s>Padmatirtha</s>, <s>Padma</s>, and <s>Pusparasagama</s>,
<s>Vrksaroha</s>, <s>Sulahara</s>, <s>Samula</s>, and <s>Sukhasambhava</s> are names.
<s>Katphala</s>, <s>Somavalka</s>, <s>Sriparni</s>, and <s>Kumuda</s>,

children.text: mahākumbhā ca kumbhīkā bhadrā bhadravatīti ca ||
children.translated_text: also <s>Mahakumbha</s>, <s>Kumbhika</s>, <s>Bhadra</s>, and <s>Bhadravati</s>, are its names.
<s>Katphala</s> removes phlegm and wind, and conquers abdominal tumors, urinary disease, and weak digestion.
It promotes appetite and removes fever, hemorrhoids, disorders of the grahani, and anemia.

children.text: devadāru smṛtaṃ dāru surāhvaṃ kilimaṃ ca tat
children.translated_text: <s>Devadaru</s> is remembered as <s>Daru</s>, <s>Surahva</s>, and <s>Kilima</s>.
It is <s>Snehaviddha</s>, <s>Mahadaru</s>, <s>Bhadradaru</s>, and <s>Indradaru</s>.
<s>Devakastha</s>, <s>Bhadrakastha</s>, <s>Putikastha</s>, and <s>Sudaru</s>,
as well as <s>Suradaru</s>, <s>Indravrksa</s>, and <s>Amaradaru</s>, are likewise its names.
<s>Devadaru</s> is bitter in taste, unctuous, hot, and conquers phlegm and wind.
It removes toxic undigested matter, constipation, abdominal distension, and urinary disorders.

children.text: kattṛṇaṃ sakalaṃ bhūti bhūtidaṃ rohiṣaṃ tṛṇam
children.translated_text: <s>Kattrna</s>, <s>Sakala</s>, <s>Bhuti</s>, <s>Bhutida</s>, and <s>Rohisa</s> grass,
<s>Dhyamaka</s>, <s>Syamaka</s>, <s>Paura</s>, <s>Patala</s>, and <s>Devadandaka</s> are its names.
<s>kattṛṇa</s> destroys asthma and cough and is especially calming for heart disease.
It removes cholera-like illness, indigestion, and colic, and destroys kapha, pitta, and disorders of the blood.

children.text: kapaṭaṃ ca sumaṅgalyaṃ ciḍā gandhavadhūs tathā
children.translated_text: <s>kapaṭa</s>, also <s>sumaṅgalya</s>, <s>ciḍā</s>, and <s>gandhavadhū</s>,
<s>taruṇa</s>, <s>taruṇī</s>, and <s>tārā</s>: it destroys disorders of wind and malignant spirits.
It removes kapha and vāta, is hot, kindles digestion, and conquers disorders of the blood.
<s>guṇṭha</s>, <s>vṛttaguṇa</s>, <s>śuṇṭha</s>, <s>śṛṅgabhedī</s>, and <s>bhamūlaka</s>,
<s>śuṇṭha</s>, <s>kuṇṭha</s>, <s>tṛṇaśuṇṭha</s>, <s>vartula</s>, and <s>pṛthukandaka</s> are names.
<s>guṇṭha</s> has an astringent aftertaste, is sweet, cooling, and relieves difficult urination.
<s>guṇṭha</s> removes bleeding disorders and purifies menstrual blood and semen.
<s>śṛṅgī</s>, <s>karkaṭaśṛṅgī</s>, <s>kulīrā</s>, and that called <s>karkaṭā</s>,
<s>kulīraśṛṅgī</s>, <s>vakrā</s>, <s>mahākoṣā</s>, and <s>natāṅginī</s>,
<s>candrāspadā</s>, <s>viṣāṇī</s>, <s>śṛṅgī</s>, and <s>vanajamūrdhajā</s> are names.
<s>karkaṭaśṛṅgī</s> is bitter and heavy, and conquers upward-moving wind.
It destroys cough, asthma, pain, and consumption, and overcomes vomiting, thirst, and loss of appetite.
<s>ajaśṛṅgī</s>, <s>meṣaśṛṅgī</s>, <s>sarpadaṃṣṭrā</s>, and <s>vartikā</s>,
<s>dvitīyā</s>, <s>dakṣiṇāvartā</s>, <s>vṛścikālī</s>, and <s>viṣāṇikā</s> are names.
<s>ajaśṛṅgī</s> is cooling and sweet, and overcomes swelling, thirst, and vomiting.
It benefits the eyes and removes asthma, heart disease, poison, cough, pain, and skin disease.
<s>śāliparṇī</s>, <s>sthirā</s>, <s>saumyā</s>, <s>triparṇī</s>, <s>atiguhā</s>, and <s>dhruvā</s>,
<s>vidārigandhā</s>, <s>aṃśumatī</s>, <s>dīrghamūlā</s>, and <s>aṃśupattrikā</s> are names.
<s>śāliparṇī</s> is bitter in taste, heavy, hot, and conquers vāta disorder.
It destroys irregular fever, urinary disorders, piles, swelling, and burning heat.
<s>ālaka</s>, <s>pālaka</s>, <s>dagdha</s>, <s>sabala</s>, and <s>bhūmigandhika</s>,

children.text: jvalanābhaṃ viśuddhaṃ ca gandhaṃ voṭaṃ kusumbhakam ||
children.translated_text: <s>jvalanābha</s>, <s>viśuddha</s>, <s>gandha</s>, <s>voṭa</s>, and <s>kusumbhaka</s> are names.
<s>pṛśniparṇī</s>, <s>pṛthakparṇī</s>, <s>kalaśī</s>, <s>dhāvanī</s>, and <s>guhā</s>,
<s>śṛgālavinnā</s>, <s>aṅghribalāparṇī</s>, and <s>kroṣṭukapucchikā</s> are names.
<s>pṛśniparṇī</s> is sweet in taste, light, hot, and conquers blood disorders and the three doṣas.
It pacifies cough and asthma and destroys fever, thirst, and burning.
<s>sarpānukāriṇī</s>, <s>tanvī</s>, <s>dīrghaparṇī</s>, and <s>parṇikā</s>,
<s>kumudā</s> and <s>atiguhā</s> too are said to be the same poison-destroying plant.

children.text: bṛhatī siṃhikā kāntā vārtākī rāṣṭrikā kulī
children.translated_text: <s>bṛhatī</s>, <s>siṃhikā</s>, <s>kāntā</s>, <s>vārtākī</s>, <s>rāṣṭrikā</s>, and <s>kulī</s>,
<s>viṣadā</s>, <s>sthūlakaṇṭākī</s>, <s>mahatī</s>, and <s>mahoṭikā</s> are names.
<s>siṃhikā</s> destroys kapha and vāta and removes asthma, colic, and fever.
It destroys vomiting, heart disease, weak digestion, and disorders from āma.

children.text: kaṇṭakārī tu duḥsparśā kṣudrā vyāghrī nidigdhikā
children.translated_text: <s>kaṇṭakārī</s> is <s>duḥsparśā</s>, <s>kṣudrā</s>, <s>vyāghrī</s>, and <s>nidigdhikā</s>,
<s>kaṇṭālikā</s>, <s>kaṇṭakinī</s>, <s>dhāvanī</s>, and <s>duṣpradharṣiṇī</s>.
<s>kaṇṭakārī</s> is pungent and bitter, hot, and conquers asthma and cough.
It destroys loss of appetite, fever, vāta and āma disorders, and heart disease.
The two kinds of <s>kaṇṭakārī</s> are bitter and conquer vāta, āma, kapha, and cough.

children.text: kṣudrikāyāḥ phalaṃ jñeyaṃ kaṭu tiktaṃ jvarāpaham ||
children.translated_text: The fruit of the small variety should be known as pungent, bitter, and fever-removing.
It destroys itching, skin disease, and worms, and likewise removes kapha and vāta.
<s>lakṣmaṇā</s>, <s>kṣetradūtī</s>, <s>sitasiṃhī</s>, and <s>kuvārtikā</s>,

children.text: suśvetā kaṇṭakārī ca durlabhā ca mahauṣadhī ||
children.translated_text: <s>suśvetā</s>, <s>kaṇṭakārī</s>, <s>durlabhā</s>, and <s>mahauṣadhī</s> are names.
It is cough-destroying; some know it as <s>kṣudramātā</s> or <s>vārtākinī</s>.
<s>vanajā</s>, somewhat <s>āṭavyā</s>, <s>kapaṭā</s>, and <s>kapaṭeśvarī</s> are names.
<s>malinā</s>, <s>malināṅgī</s>, and also <s>kaṭuvārttākinī</s>,
<s>gardabhī</s>, <s>bahuvāhā</s>, <s>candrapuṣpā</s>, and <s>priyaṃkarī</s> are names.

children.text: vṛntākī vārttikā vṛntā bhaṇṭākī bhaṇṭikā matā
children.translated_text: <s>vṛntākī</s>, <s>vārttikā</s>, <s>vṛntā</s>, <s>bhaṇṭākī</s>, and <s>bhaṇṭikā</s> are accepted names.
<s>vṛntāka</s> is sweet, sharp, hot, pungent in digestion, and not aggravating to pitta.
It removes kapha and vāta, is good for the heart, kindles digestion, promotes semen, and is light.
<s>gokṣura</s> is also <s>gokṣuraka</s>, <s>bhakṣaka</s>, and <s>svādukaṇṭaka</s>.
<s>gokaṇṭaka</s>, <s>bhakṣaṭaka</s>, <s>ṣaḍaṅga</s>, and <s>kaṇṭakatrika</s> are names.
<s>śvadaṃṣṭra</s> is nourishing, aphrodisiac, calming to the three doṣas, and kindles digestion.
It destroys colic, heart disease, and urinary difficulty, and removes prameha.
<s>bilva</s>, <s>śalāṭu</s>, <s>śāṇḍilya</s>, <s>hṛdyagandha</s>, and <s>mahāphala</s>,
<s>śailūṣa</s>, <s>śrīphala</s>, <s>śryāhva</s>, <s>karkaṭa</s>, and <s>pūtimāruta</s>,
<s>lakṣmīphala</s>, <s>gandhagarbha</s>, <s>satyakarmā</s>, and <s>durāruha</s>,
<s>vātasāra</s>, <s>arimeda</s>, <s>kaṇṭakāḍhya</s>, and <s>asitānana</s> are names.
<s>bilva</s> root destroys the three doṣas and vomiting; it is sweet and light.

children.text: bilvasya tu phalaṃ bālaṃ snigdhaṃ saṃgrāhi dīpanam ||
children.translated_text: The unripe fruit of <s>bilva</s> is unctuous, binding, and digestive-kindling.
It is pungent, bitter, astringent, hot, sharp, and removes vāta and kapha.
The same fruit when fully ripe should be known as having a sweet aftertaste and as heavy.
It causes burning and constipation, removes doṣas, and dispels foul wind.
<s>agnimantha</s>, <s>agnimathana</s>, <s>tarkārī</s>, and <s>vaijayantikā</s>,
<s>vahnimantha</s>, <s>araṇī</s>, <s>ketu</s>, <s>śrīparṇī</s>, <s>karṇikā</s>, and <s>jayā</s>,
<s>nādeyī</s>, <s>vahnimathana</s>, and secondly <s>agnimanthana</s>,
<s>raktāṅga</s>, <s>manthana</s>, and that same <s>araṇika</s> are accepted names.
<s>tarkārī</s> is pungent, bitter, hot, and conquers vāta and pallor.
It destroys swelling, kapha, weak digestive fire, āma, and constipation.
<s>śyonāka</s>, <s>śukanāsa</s>, <s>kaṭvaṅga</s>, and <s>kaṭaṃbhara</s>,
<s>mayūrajaṅgha</s>, <s>araluka</s>, <s>priyajīva</s>, and <s>kuṭannaṭa</s>,
It is called <s>pṛthuśimba</s>, <s>ṭiṇṭuka</s>, and <s>dīrghavṛntaka</s>.
<s>bhallūka</s>, <s>śillaka</s>, <s>phalguvṛntāka</s>, and <s>jambuka</s> are accepted names.
<s>ṭiṇṭuka</s> is cooling, bitter, and an excellent remover of bladder disease.
It conquers pitta, kapha, āma, vāta, diarrhea, cough, and loss of appetite.
<s>kāśmaryā</s>, <s>kāśmarī</s>, <s>hīrā</s>, <s>kāśmaryā</s>, and also <s>madhuparṇī</s>,
<s>śrīparṇī</s>, <s>sarvatobhadrā</s>, <s>gambhārī</s>, and <s>kṛṣṇavṛntakā</s> are names.
<s>śrīparṇī</s> is bitter in its own juice, heavy, hot, and conquers bleeding disorders.
It conquers disorders of the three <s>doṣas</s>, fatigue, burning pain, fever, thirst, and poison.
The <s>pāṭalā</s> mentioned is also <s>kumbhīkā</s>, <s>tāmrapuṣpā</s>, and <s>ambuvāsinī</s>.
It is <s>sthālī</s>, <s>vasantadūtī</s>, <s>amoghā</s>, and <s>kālavṛntikā</s>.

children.text: pāṭalā tu rase tiktā gurūṣṇā pavanāsrajit
children.translated_text: <s>Pāṭalā</s> is bitter in taste, heavy, hot, and conquers wind and blood disorders.
It destroys bilious disorders, hiccup, vomiting, swelling, phlegm, and anorexia.
A second <s>pāṭalā</s>, white in color, is specified as <s>kāṣṭhapāṭalā</s>.
It is also <s>śvetakumbhīkā</s>, <s>kuberākṣī</s>, and <s>phaleruhā</s>.

children.text: pāṭalāyāḥ guṇais tadvat kiṃcin mārutakṛd bhavet
children.translated_text: It has the same qualities as <s>pāṭalā</s>, but may produce a little wind.
<s>Jīvaka</s> is <s>śṛṅgaka</s>, <s>kṣveḍa</s>, <s>dīrghāyu</s>, and <s>kūrcaśīrṣaka</s>.
It is <s>hrasvāṅga</s>, sweet and pleasant, life-giving, and also long-lived.
<s>Jīvaka</s> is sweet and cooling; it conquers bleeding disorders, pitta, and wind.
It removes burning, fever, and wasting, and increases phlegm and semen.

children.text: ṛṣabho durdharo dhīro mātṛko vṛṣabho vṛṣaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Ṛṣabha</s> is <s>durdhara</s>, <s>dhīra</s>, <s>mātṛka</s>, <s>vṛṣabha</s>, and <s>vṛṣa</s>.
It is also <s>viṣāṇī</s>, <s>kakud</s>, <s>indrākṣa</s>, <s>bandhura</s>, and <s>gopati</s>.
<s>Ṛṣabha</s> is sweet in taste and removes pitta, blood disorders, and wind.
It removes wasting, burning, and fever, and increases phlegm and semen.

children.text: medā jñeyā maṇicchidrā śalyaparṇī dharāpi ca
children.translated_text: <s>Medā</s> should be known as <s>maṇicchidrā</s>, <s>śalyaparṇī</s>, and also <s>dharā</s>.
<s>Mahāmedā</s> is called <s>devamaṇi</s> and <s>vasucchidrā</s>.
<s>Medā</s> is sweet in taste and cooling; it removes wasting, burning, and fever.

children.text: sā pittaṃ tu jayecchukraṃ sakaphaṃ ca vivardhayet ||
children.translated_text: It conquers pitta and increases semen together with phlegm.
<s>Mahāmedā</s> is cooling and sweet, and increases phlegm and semen.
It removes burning, blood disorders, and pitta, along with wasting, wind, and fever.
<s>Vijayā</s> is <s>rañjikā</s>, <s>bhaṅgā</s>, sleep-inducing, and much-speaking.
It is called <s>mādinī</s>, <s>mādikā</s>, <s>mātuḥ</s>, and also <s>gañjākinī</s>.

children.text: bhaṅgā kaphaharī tiktā grāhiṇī yācanī laghuḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Bhaṅgā</s> removes phlegm, is bitter, astringent in effect, stimulating, and light.
It is sharp and hot, produces pitta, and increases delusion, intoxication, speech, and digestive fire.

children.text: kākolī madhurā śuklā kṣīrā dhvāṅkṣolikā smṛtā
children.translated_text: <s>Kākolī</s> is sweet, white, milky, and remembered as <s>dhvāṅkṣolikā</s>.

children.text: vayaḥsthā svādumāṃsī ca vāyasolī ca karṇikā ||
children.translated_text: It is <s>vayaḥsthā</s>, <s>svādumāṃsī</s>, <s>vāyasolī</s>, and <s>karṇikā</s>.
<s>Kākolī</s> is sweet and cooling, and removes wind, pitta, and fever.
It removes burning and wasting, and increases phlegm and semen.
The second, <s>kṣīrakākolī</s>, is <s>kṣīraśuklā</s> and <s>payasvinī</s>.
It is <s>vayaḥsthā</s>, milk-sweet, strong, and <s>kṣīraviṣāṇikā</s>.
It is considered pleasing to the taste and calming to wind, pitta, blood disorders, and heart disease.
It removes dyspnea, cough, and wasting, is aphrodisiac, and purifies the bladder.
<s>Māṣaparṇī</s> is <s>kāmbojī</s>, <s>kṛṣṇavṛntā</s>, and <s>mahāsahā</s>.
It is <s>ārdramāṣā</s>, <s>siṃhavinnā</s>, <s>māṃsamāṣā</s>, and <s>aśvapucchikā</s>.
<s>Māṣaparṇī</s> is bitter in taste, cooling, and conquers bleeding disorders and pitta.
It produces phlegm and semen, is sweet, and removes burning, fever, and wind.
<s>Mudgaparṇī</s> is <s>kṣudrasahā</s>, <s>śimbī</s>, and <s>mārjāragandhikā</s>.
<s>Vanajā</s>, <s>riṅgaṇī</s>, <s>hrasvā</s>, and the two <s>śūrpaparṇī</s>s are remembered.
<s>Mudgaparṇī</s> is cooling and sweet, and destroys wind and blood disorders.
It removes pitta, burning, and fever, kills worms, and produces phlegm and semen.
<s>Jīvantī</s> is <s>jīvanīyā</s>, <s>jīvanī</s>, and <s>jīvavardhanī</s>.
It has the auspicious name, is the best of vegetables, and is fame-giving.
<s>Jīvantī</s> is good for the eyes, destroys all doṣas, is sweet, and cooling.

children.text: śākānāṃ pravarā nyūnā dvitīyā kiṃcideva tu ||
children.translated_text: It is the foremost among vegetables; the second variety is only slightly inferior.

children.text: madhuyaṣṭī ca yaṣṭī ca yaṣṭīmadhu madhusravā
children.translated_text: <s>Madhuyaṣṭī</s> is <s>yaṣṭī</s>, <s>yaṣṭīmadhu</s>, and <s>madhusravā</s>.
It is <s>yaṣṭīka</s>, <s>madhuka</s>, <s>yaṣṭyāhva</s>, and <s>madhuyaṣṭikā</s>.
One kind grows on land, another in water; it is also <s>madhuparṇī</s> and <s>madhūlikā</s>.
<s>Madhuyaṣṭī</s> is sweet in taste, cooling, and destroys pitta.
It is aphrodisiac, removes drying and wasting, and destroys poison and vomiting.

children.text: tallakṣaṇaṃ klītanakaṃ klītanaṃ klītikā ca sā
children.translated_text: That kind is marked as <s>klītanaka</s>, <s>klītana</s>, and <s>klītikā</s>.
The pair of <s>yaṣṭikā</s>s is sweet, conquers thirst, pitta, and blood disorders, and is cooling.

children.text: ṛddhirvṛddhiḥ sukhaṃ siddhī rathāṅgaṃ maṅgalaṃ vasu
children.translated_text: <s>Ṛddhi</s> is <s>vṛddhi</s>, <s>sukha</s>, <s>siddhi</s>, <s>rathāṅga</s>, <s>maṅgala</s>, and <s>vasu</s>.
It is <s>ṛṣisṛṣṭā</s>, <s>yuga</s>, <s>yogya</s>, <s>lakṣmī</s>, and dear to all people.
<s>Ṛddhi</s> is sweet and cooling; it conquers wasting, pitta, and wind.
It removes blood disorders and fever, and increases phlegm and semen.
<s>Vidārikā</s> is considered white, sweet-tubered, and <s>śṛgālikā</s>.
It is <s>vṛṣyakandā</s>, <s>vidārī</s>, <s>vṛṣyavallī</s>, and <s>viḍālikā</s>.
<s>Vidārī</s> is cooling, sweet, heavy, unctuous, and conquers wind.
It conquers pitta and blood disorders, and is also described as strengthening and aphrodisiac.
Another, which is <s>kṣīravidārī</s>, is also <s>ikṣugandhā</s> and <s>ikṣuvallyā</s>.
It is <s>kṣīravallī</s>, <s>kṣīrakandā</s>, <s>kṣīraśuklā</s>, and <s>payasvinī</s>.
<s>Kṣīravidārikā</s> is strengthening and removes wind and pitta.
It is sweet, nourishing, aphrodisiac, cool to the touch, and very diuretic.
It removes disorders of breast milk and destroys bilious colic.
<s>Kapikacchū</s> is <s>ātmaguptā</s>, <s>svayaṃguptā</s>, and <s>maharṣabhī</s>.
It is <s>lāṅgūlī</s>, <s>kaṇḍulā</s>, <s>caṇḍā</s>, <s>markaṭī</s>, and hard to handle.
<s>Kapikacchū</s> is sweet and bitter in taste, cooling, and removes wind.
It is aphrodisiac, removes pitta and blood disorders, and destroys foul ulcers.
<s>Dadhipuṣpī</s> is <s>khaṭvāṅgī</s>, <s>khaṭvā</s>, and <s>paryaṅkapādikā</s>.

children.text: ṛṣabhī sā tu kākāṇḍī jñeyā śūkarapādikā ||
children.translated_text: It is <s>ṛṣabhī</s>, and should be known as <s>kākāṇḍī</s> and <s>śūkarapādikā</s>.
<s>Kākāṇḍī</s> removes phlegm and pitta, is heavy, coloring, and destroys wind.
It has hot potency and sweet taste; it is like <s>māṣa</s>.
<s>Śitivāra</s> is <s>sūcipatra</s>, <s>sūcyāhva</s>, and <s>suniṣaṇṇaka</s>.
It is <s>śrīvāraka</s>, <s>śitivara</s>, <s>svastika</s>, <s>kukkuṭa</s>, and <s>śikhī</s>.
<s>Śitivāra</s> is constipating, astringent, and conquers all doṣas.
It is excellent for purifying heart disease, spleen disorders, abdominal lumps, piles, and the bladder.
<s>Pāṣāṇabhedaka</s> is <s>aśmaghna</s>, <s>śilābheda</s>, and <s>aśmabhedaka</s>.
It is also <s>upalabheda</s>, <s>nagabhid</s>, <s>dṛṣad</s>, and <s>aśmajit</s>.
<s>Aśmabheda</s> is cool and bitter, and conquers gravel and pain of the penis.
It is supreme for heart disease, spleen disease, gulma, piles, and for cleansing the bladder.
<s>Śrāvaṇī</s> is <s>Muṇḍitikā</s>, <s>Bhikṣu</s>, and <s>Śravaṇaśīrṣikā</s>.
Called <s>Śravaṇā</s>, it is also <s>Pravrajitā</s>, <s>Parivrājī</s>, and <s>Tapodhanā</s>.
<s>Mahāśrāvaṇikā</s>, <s>Muṇḍī</s>, <s>Lobhanīyā</s>, and likewise another name,
<s>Kadambapuṣpikā</s>, are taught; she is also <s>Chinnagranthinikā</s>.
<s>Muṇḍikā</s> is pungent and bitter, and destroys vāta and blood disorders.
It destroys āma, anorexia, epilepsy, goiter, and elephantiasis.
<s>Sārivā</s> is <s>Śāradā</s>, <s>Gopā</s>, <s>Gopavallī</s>, and <s>Pratānikā</s>.
It is called <s>Gopakanyā</s>, <s>Latāsphotā</s>, the white variety, and <s>Kāṣṭhasārivā</s>.
Another <s>Sārivā</s> is <s>Kṛṣṇamūlī</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇā</s>, and <s>Candanasārivā</s>.
It is <s>Bhadrā</s>, <s>Candanagopā</s>, <s>Candanā</s>, and also <s>Kṛṣṇavallī</s>.
The two <s>Sārivā</s> plants are sweet and destroy kapha, vāta, and blood disorders.
They remove skin disease, itching, and fever, and destroy urinary disease and foul odor.
<s>Kṛṣṇamūlī</s> is constipating, cooling, and conquers kapha and vāta.
It is remembered as calming thirst and anorexia and removing raktapitta (bleeding disorder).
<s>Vākucī</s> is <s>Somarājī</s>, <s>Somavallī</s>, and also <s>Suvallī</s>.
It is <s>Avalgujā</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇaphalā</s>, and the same is considered <s>Pūtiphalā</s>.

children.text: candralekhendulekhā ca śaśilekhā matā ca sā
children.translated_text: It is also considered <s>Candralekhā</s>, <s>Indulekhā</s>, and <s>Śaśilekhā</s>.
It is <s>Pūtikarṇī</s>, <s>Kālameṣī</s>, foul-smelling, and destroyer of skin disease.
<s>Vākucī</s> is cooling and bitter; it conquers phlegm, skin disease, and worms.
Used as a rasāyana (rejuvenative), it increases taste and intelligence.

children.text: madanaḥ śalyako rāṭhaḥ piṇḍī piṇḍītakaḥ phalaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Madana</s> is <s>Śalyaka</s>, <s>Rāṭha</s>, <s>Piṇḍī</s>, <s>Piṇḍītaka</s>, and <s>Phala</s>.
It is <s>Gālava</s>, <s>Karahāṭa</s>, <s>Chardana</s>, and <s>Viṣapuṣpaka</s>.
<s>Madana</s> is pungent, bitter, hot, and removes wounds.
In phlegmatic fever, coryza, gulma, and abscesses,
it removes swelling and morbid doṣas; here it is praised for use in the bladder and for emesis.

children.text: kaṭukālāmbunī tumbī lambā piṇḍaphalā ca sā
children.translated_text: <s>Kaṭukālāmbunī</s>, <s>Tumbī</s>, <s>Lambā</s>, and <s>Piṇḍaphalā</s> are its names.
<s>Ikṣvāku</s> is <s>Kṣatriyavarā</s>, <s>Tiktabījā</s>, and <s>Mahāphalā</s>.
It removes cough, asthma, and vomiting in one afflicted by poison and emaciated by kapha.
<s>Ikṣvāku</s> is excellent for emesis when a person is fainting.
<s>Kaṭutumbī</s> is pungent and bitter; it produces vāta and conquers asthma and cough.
It destroys kapha, purifies, and removes swelling, wounds, pain, and poison.
<s>Jīmūtaka</s> is <s>Devatāḍa</s>, <s>Vṛttakośa</s>, and <s>Garāgarī</s>.
It is said to be <s>Ākhuviṣahā</s>, <s>Veṇī</s>, <s>Devadālī</s>, and <s>Tāḍakā</s>.
<s>Jīmūtaka</s>, in fever, asthma, cough, hiccup, anorexia, and wasting,
destroys swelling, pallor, and poison; it is beneficial in artificial poisons and for emesis.
<s>Trapusa</s> is pungent, bitter, pale, and called <s>Hastiparṇinī</s>.
It is also <s>Dīrghaparṇī</s>, <s>Mūtraphalā</s>, and <s>Latākarkaṭikā</s>.
<s>Trapusa</s> is said to remove vomiting and to cleanse the bladder.

children.text: urvāruḥ karkaṭī proktā vyālapattrā ca lomaśā
children.translated_text: <s>Urvāru</s> is called <s>Karkaṭī</s>, <s>Vyālapattrā</s>, and <s>Lomaśā</s>.
It is <s>Sthūlā</s>, <s>Toyaphalā</s>, <s>Hastidantaphalā</s>, and <s>Muni</s>.

children.text: urvārukaṃ pittaharaṃ suśītalaṃ mūtrāmayaghnaṃ madhuraṃ rucipradam
children.translated_text: <s>Urvāruka</s> removes pitta, is very cooling, destroys urinary disorders, is sweet, and gives appetite.

children.text: saṃtāpamūrcchāpaharaṃ sutṛptidaṃ vātaprakopāya ghanaṃ tu sevitam ||
children.translated_text: It removes burning and fainting and gives full satisfaction; when consumed in excess it provokes vāta.

children.text: vālukaṃ kāṇḍakaṃ vālu tacchītaṃ madhuraṃ guru
children.translated_text: <s>Vāluka</s>, <s>Kāṇḍaka</s>, or <s>Vālu</s> is cooling, sweet, and heavy.
It removes raktapitta and is laxative; when ripe it is light, hot, and kindles digestive fire.
<s>Śīrṇavṛnta</s> is <s>Citraphala</s>, variegated, and yellow-colored.
<s>Śīrṇavṛnta</s> is light, sweet, laxative, hot, and produces digestive fire and pitta.
<s>Cirbhaṭa</s>, also called <s>Dhenudugdha</s>, should be known as <s>Gorakṣakarkaṭī</s>.
<s>Cirbhaṭa</s> is sweet, dry, heavy, and removes pitta and kapha.
<s>Ḍaṅgarī</s>, <s>Ḍāṅgarī</s>, <s>Dīrghorvāru</s>, and <s>Ḍaṅgari</s> are names.
It is <s>Ḍāṅgārī</s>, <s>Nāgaśuṇḍī</s>, <s>Gajadantaphalā</s>, and <s>Muni</s>.
<s>Ḍaṅgarī</s> is cooling and appetizing, and conquers burning, pitta, and blood disorders.
It removes wasting, nourishes and strengthens, removes dullness, and relieves retention of urine.
<s>Kūṣmāṇḍikā</s> is considered <s>Kumbhaphalā</s> and <s>Sthiraphalā</s>.

children.text: kūṣmāṇḍī somasṛṣṭā ca pītikā ca bṛhatphalā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kūṣmāṇḍī</s> is <s>Somasṛṣṭā</s>, <s>Pītikā</s>, and <s>Bṛhatphalā</s>.
Among vine-fruits, <s>Kūṣmāṇḍa</s> is foremost and conquers vāta and pitta.
It cleanses the bladder, is aphrodisiac, beneficial to the heart, and conquers disorders of the mind.
<s>Vandhyakarkoṭakī</s> is <s>Devī</s>, <s>Manojñā</s>, and <s>Kumārikā</s>.
It is <s>Nāgāri</s>, <s>Sarpadamanī</s>, and also <s>Viṣakaṇṭakinī</s>.
It should be known as <s>Nāgadamanī</s> and <s>Sarvabhūtapramardinī</s>.
It is also known as <s>Vandhyāputrapradā</s> and <s>Yogeśvarī</s>.
<s>Karkoṭakī</s> has sweet fruit and is <s>Manojñā</s> and <s>Kumārikā</s>.

children.text: avandhyā caiva devī ca viṣapraśamanī tathā ||
children.translated_text: It is also <s>Avandhyā</s>, <s>Devī</s>, and a pacifier of poison.
The pair of <s>Karkoṭakī</s> plants is bitter and destroys both kapha and poison.
With honey, its root is praised for diseases of the head.
<s>Dhāmārgava</s> is <s>Kośaphalā</s> and also <s>Rājakośātakī</s>.
It is called <s>Karkoṭakī</s>, <s>Pītapuṣpā</s>, and <s>Mahājālinī</s>.
Another <s>Mahākośātakī</s> is <s>Hastighoṣā</s> and <s>Mahāphalā</s>.

children.text: dhāmārgavo gadeṣviṣṭaḥ sthireṣu ca mahatsu ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Dhāmārgava</s> is desired in diseases that are fixed and great.
<s>Kośātakī</s> is very bitter and hot, and purifies the large and small intestines.
It is used in cough, gulma, abdominal disease, artificial poison, and when vāta is lodged in the seat of kapha,
and when kapha is situated in the throat and mouth and in accumulations of kapha.

children.text: anyā svādus tridoṣaghnī jvarasyānte hitā smṛtā ||
children.translated_text: Another kind is sweet, destroys the three doṣas, and is remembered as beneficial at the end of fever.
<s>Kośātakī</s> is <s>Kṛtacchidrā</s>, <s>Jālinī</s>, and <s>Kṛtavedhanī</s>.
It is considered <s>Kṣveḍā</s>, very bitter, <s>Ghaṇṭālī</s>, and <s>Mṛdaṅgaphalikā</s>.
<s>Kṣveḍa</s> is bitter, pungent, sharp, and suitable when the disease is not deep-seated.
It is praised in skin disease, pallor, disease, spleen disorder, swelling, gulma, artificial poison, and the like.
<s>Aśmantaka</s>, <s>Candraka</s>, <s>Kuddālī</s>, and <s>Amlapattraka</s> are names.
<s>Mālukāparṇa</s>, having smooth bark, is remembered as <s>Yamalapattraka</s>.
<s>Aśmantaka</s> is astringent, cooling, and removes pitta and phlegm.
It is sweet, cooling, constipating, and conquers burning, thirst, and urinary disease.
For <s>Kovidāra</s>, there are <s>Kuddāla</s>, <s>Kumbhāra</s>, <s>Kuṇḍalī</s>, and <s>Kulī</s>.
It is <s>Tāmrapuṣpa</s>, <s>Camarika</s>, and <s>Mahāyamalapattraka</s>.
<s>Kovidāra</s> is astringent, constipating, and heals wounds.
It pacifies scrofulous swellings and prolapse of the anus, and removes skin disease and disorders of the hair.
<s>Āvartakī</s> is <s>Bindukinī</s>, <s>Vibhāṇḍī</s>, and <s>Pītakīlakā</s>.
It is called <s>Carmaraṅgā</s>, <s>Pītapuṣpā</s>, and <s>Mahājālinī</s>.
<s>Āvartakī</s> destroys skin disease and removes both upward and downward doṣas.
It is astringent, cooling, aphrodisiac, destroys the three doṣas, and conquers diarrhea.
It destroys swelling, abdominal lumps, abdominal enlargement, distension, and clusters of worms.
<s>Śaṇapuṣpī</s> and <s>Bṛhatpuṣpī</s> are also called <s>Śaṇaghaṇṭikā</s>.
<s>Mahāśaṇa</s> is <s>Mālyapuṣpī</s>, emetic, pungent, and bitter.
<s>Śaṇapuṣpī</s> is bitter in taste, emetic, and conquers phlegm and pitta.
It destroys wind, and diseases of the throat, heart, and mouth.

children.text: bimbī raktaphalā tuṇḍī tuṇḍikeraphalā ca sā
children.translated_text: <s>Bimbī</s> is <s>Raktaphalā</s>, <s>Tuṇḍī</s>, and also <s>Tuṇḍikeraphalā</s>.
It is <s>Oṣṭhopamaphalā</s>, <s>Golhā</s>, <s>Pīluparṇī</s>, and <s>Tuṇḍikā</s>.
<s>Tuṇḍikā</s> removes phlegm, pitta, blood disorder, swelling, pallor, and fever.
It removes dyspnea and cough; its fruit brings about wind and phlegm.
<s>Harītakī</s> is <s>Abhayā</s>, <s>Pathyā</s>, <s>Prapathyā</s>, <s>Pūtanā</s>, and <s>Amṛtā</s>.
It is <s>Jayā</s>, <s>Avyathā</s>, <s>Haimavatī</s>, <s>Vayaḥsthā</s>, <s>Cetakī</s>, and <s>Śivā</s>.

children.text: prāṇadā nandinī caiva rohiṇī vijayā ca sā
children.translated_text: It is <s>Prāṇadā</s>, <s>Nandinī</s>, <s>Rohiṇī</s>, and also <s>Vijayā</s>.
It is astringent, sour, pungent, bitter, and furnished with sweet taste.
Thus <s>Pathyā</s> has five tastes, being devoid of salt.
Because of its sour character it conquers wind; because of sweetness and bitterness, pitta.
Because of dryness and astringency it conquers phlegm; therefore <s>Abhayā</s> destroys the three doṣas.

children.text: prapathyā lekhanī laghvī medhyā cakṣurhitā sadā
children.translated_text: <s>Prapathyā</s> is scraping, light, good for the intellect, and always beneficial for the eyes.
It conquers urinary disease, skin disease, wounds, vomiting, swelling, wind, blood disorder, and dysuria.
<s>Harītakī</s> directs wind downward, is cordial, and clarifies the senses.
It generally destroys diseases produced by over-nourishment.
In thirst, dryness of the mouth, stiffness of the jaw, and constriction of the throat,

children.text: navajvare tathā kṣīṇe garbhiṇyāṃ na praśasyate ||
children.translated_text: as well as in fresh fever, in an emaciated person, and in a pregnant woman, it is not recommended.

children.text: harasya bhavane jātā haritā ca svabhāvataḥ
children.translated_text: It was born in <s>Hara</s>'s abode and is by nature greenish.

children.text: sarvarogāṃśca ca harate tena khyātā harītakī ||
children.translated_text: Because it removes all diseases, it is famous as <s>Harītakī</s>.
<s>Vibhītaka</s> is <s>Karṣaphala</s>, <s>Vāsanta</s>, <s>Akṣa</s>, and <s>Kalidruma</s>.
It is <s>Saṃvartaka</s>, <s>Bhūtavāsa</s>, <s>Kalkihārya</s>, and <s>Baheḍaka</s>.
<s>Vibhītaka</s> is pungent in digestion, light, conquers hoarseness, and is laxative.
It destroys cough and diseases of the eyes and mouth, and is especially productive of hair growth.
<s>Āmalaka</s> is <s>Vayaḥsthā</s>, aphrodisiac, with the taste of nutmeg, and auspicious.
It is remembered as <s>Dhātrīphala</s>, <s>Śrīphala</s>, and likewise <s>Amṛtaphala</s>.
<s>Āmalaka</s> is astringent, pungent, bitter, sour, and sweet, and is cooling.

children.text: saraṃ tridoṣahṛd vṛṣyaṃ jvaraghnaṃ ca rasāyanam ||
children.translated_text: It is laxative, removes the three doṣas, is aphrodisiac, fever-destroying, and a rejuvenative.
Because of its sourness it destroys wind; because of sweetness and coolness, pitta.
Because of dryness and astringency the fruit of <s>Dhātrī</s> conquers phlegm and the three doṣas.
<s>Prācīnāmalaka</s>, <s>Prācīnāraṅga</s>, and <s>Raktaka</s> are considered the same.
When ripe, it produces pitta and phlegm, is hard to digest, heavy, and conquers wind.
<s>Āragvadha</s> is <s>Dīrghaphala</s>, <s>Vyādhihā</s>, and <s>Caturaṅgula</s>.
It is also <s>Ārevata</s>, <s>Karṇī</s>, <s>Karṇikāra</s>, and <s>Recana</s>.
<s>Āragvadha</s> is bitter in taste, heavy, hot, and removes worms and colic.
It destroys phlegm, abdominal disease, and urinary disease, and conquers dysuria, abdominal lumps, and the three doṣas.
<s>Karṇikāra</s> is <s>Rājavṛkṣa</s>, <s>Pragraha</s>, and <s>Kṛtamālaka</s>.
It is <s>Ārogyaśimbī</s>, <s>Śampāka</s>, <s>Vyādhighāta</s>, and <s>Vyathāntaka</s>.

children.text: kṛtamālo laghuḥ śītaḥ pittaghno madhuraḥ saraḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛtamāla</s> is light, cooling, pitta-destroying, sweet, and laxative.
Its fruit is sweet, strengthening, conquers wind, pitta, and undigested matter, and is laxative.

children.text: dantī śīghrā nikumbhā syād upacitrā mukūlakaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Dantī</s> is <s>Śīghrā</s>, <s>Nikumbhā</s>, <s>Upacitrā</s>, and <s>Mukūlaka</s>.
It is also <s>Udumbaraparṇī</s>, <s>Viśalyā</s>, and <s>Ghuṇapriyā</s>.
<s>Dantī</s> is sharp, hot, and pungent, and conquers phlegm, wind, and abdominal disease.
It destroys piles, wounds, stones, and colic; it kindles digestion and purifies.

children.text: varaṇī ca varāṅgī ca tathaiva ca jayāvahā
children.translated_text: <s>Varaṇī</s> is also <s>Varāṅgī</s> and likewise <s>Jayāvahā</s>.
It is <s>Āvartakī</s>, <s>Keśaruhā</s>, and likewise <s>Viṣabhadrikā</s>.
<s>Varaṇī</s> is bitter in taste and destroys colic and disorders of the skin.
It destroys phlegm, wind, abdominal disease, and piles; it kindles digestion and purifies.
<s>Jayapāla</s> is purgative, laxative, and the fruit of <s>Tintiḍī</s>.
It is <s>Dantībīja</s>, liquefies the feces, and is <s>Nikumbha</s>, the purgative seed.
<s>Kumbhībīja</s> and the seed called <s>Nikumbha</s> are that fruit of <s>Kumbhinī</s>.
<s>Jepāla</s> is pungent and hot, removes worms, and is purgative.
It kindles digestion, destroys phlegm and wind, and removes abdominal disease.
<s>Dravantī</s> is <s>Śambarī</s>, <s>Citrā</s>, <s>Nyagrodhā</s>, and <s>Mūṣakāhvayā</s>.
It is <s>Pratyakśreṇī</s>, <s>Vṛṣā</s>, <s>Caṇḍā</s>, <s>Putraśreṇī</s>, and <s>Ākhuparṇikā</s>.
<s>Dravantī</s> is beneficial in grahaṇī disease, thirst, and the calming of the three doṣas.
It is useful in a body affected by obstruction, in glandular swellings, urinary disease, abdominal disease, and poison.
In diseases of phlegm and pitta, pallor, worms in the bowel, and fistula,
<s>Dravantī</s> removes heart disease and destroys phlegm and worms.

children.text: nīlinī nīlikā kālā grāmyā dolā viśodhanī
children.translated_text: <s>Nīlinī</s> is <s>Nīlikā</s>, <s>Kālā</s>, <s>Grāmyā</s>, <s>Dolā</s>, and <s>Viśodhanī</s>.

children.text: tutthā śrīphalikā mocā bhāravāhī ca rañjanī ||
children.translated_text: It is <s>Tutthā</s>, <s>Śrīphalikā</s>, <s>Mocā</s>, <s>Bhāravāhī</s>, and <s>Rañjanī</s>.
<s>Nīlī</s> is bitter in taste and hot, and removes disease of the waist, wind, and phlegm.
It is good for the hair, destroys poison and abdominal disease, and removes wind, blood disorder, and worms.

children.text: snuk snuhī ca mahāvṛkṣo guḍā nistriṃśapattrakaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Snuk</s>, <s>Snuhī</s>, <s>Mahāvṛkṣa</s>, <s>Guḍā</s>, and <s>Nistriṃśapattraka</s>,
as well as <s>Samantadugdhā</s>, <s>Gaṇḍīra</s>, <s>Sehuṇḍa</s>, and <s>Vajrakaṇṭaka</s>.
<s>Sehuṇḍa</s> is bitter in taste, heavy and hot, and conquers phlegm and wind.
It destroys foul ulcers and urinary stones, and likewise purifies wind.
The milky sap of <s>snuhī</s> is supreme for removing poison, distension, abdominal lumps, and abdominal disease.
<s>Sātalā</s> is <s>saptalā</s>, <s>sārī</s>, <s>vidulā</s>, <s>vimalā</s>, and <s>amalā</s>.
It is <s>bahuphenā</s>, <s>carmakaṣā</s>, <s>phenā</s>, <s>dīptā</s>, and <s>marālikā</s>.
<s>Sātalā</s> is purifying and bitter, and removes disorders of phlegm, pitta, and blood.
It removes swelling, abdominal disease, and distension, but may produce a little wind.
<s>Kṣīriṇī</s> is <s>kāñcanakṣīrī</s>, <s>kaṭuparṇī</s>, and <s>karṣaṇī</s>.
It is <s>tiktadugdhā</s>, <s>haimavatī</s>, <s>hemadugdhā</s>, and <s>himāvatī</s>.
<s>Kāñcanakṣīrī</s> is bitter and removes pitta, worms, and poison.
It is purifying, calms accumulations of doṣas, and conquers bleeding disorders.
<s>Svarṇakṣīrī</s> is <s>svarṇadugdhā</s> and also <s>suvarṇakṣīrikā</s>.
It is called <s>hemāhvā</s>, <s>kanakakṣīrī</s>, <s>hemakṣīrī</s>, and <s>kāñcanī</s>.
The pair of <s>kṣīriṇī</s>s is bitter and removes worms, pitta, and phlegm.
<s>Śyāmā</s> is <s>trivṛt</s>, <s>mālavikā</s>, and <s>masūravidalā</s>.
It is <s>kālārdhacandrā</s>, <s>pālindī</s>, <s>suṣeṇī</s>, and also <s>kālameṣī</s>.
<s>Trivṛt</s> is pungent and hot, and destroys worms, phlegm, abdominal disease, and fever.
It destroys swelling, anemia, and spleen disorders, and is the best for purgation.

children.text: śuklabhaṇḍī tribhaṇḍī syāt kākākṣī saralā trivṛt
children.translated_text: <s>Śuklabhaṇḍī</s> is <s>tribhaṇḍī</s>, <s>kākākṣī</s>, <s>saralā</s>, and <s>trivṛt</s>.
It is <s>sarvānubhūti</s>, <s>tripuṭā</s>, <s>tryasrā</s>, and <s>kumudagandhinī</s>.

children.text: kaṣāyā madhurā coṣṇā vipāke kaṭukā trivṛt
children.translated_text: <s>Trivṛt</s> is astringent and sweet, hot, and pungent in post-digestive effect.
It calms phlegm and pitta, is dry, and provokes wind.
<s>Aindrī</s>, <s>indravāruṇī</s>, <s>indrāhvā</s>, and <s>indravāru</s> are names; it is <s>mṛgādanī</s>.
It is <s>gavādanī</s>, <s>kṣudraphalā</s>, <s>vṛṣabhākṣī</s>, and also <s>gavākṣī</s>.
<s>Indravāruṇikā</s> is very hot, purgative, and also pungent.
It destroys worms, phlegm, and ulcers, and also destroys all abdominal diseases.
Another <s>indravāruṇī</s> is said to be <s>viśālā</s> and <s>mahāphalā</s>.

children.text: ātmarakṣā citraphalā trapusī trapusā ca sā ||
children.translated_text: It is <s>ātmarakṣā</s>, <s>citraphalā</s>, <s>trapusī</s>, and <s>trapusā</s>.

children.text: indravārudvayaṃ tiktaṃ kaṭu pāke rase laghu
children.translated_text: The two <s>indravāru</s>s are bitter, pungent in post-digestive effect and taste, and light.
They are hot in potency and destroy jaundice, pitta, phlegm, and elephantiasis.
<s>Śvetapuṣpī</s>, <s>mṛgākṣī</s>, <s>mṛgairvāru</s>, and <s>mṛgādanī</s> are names.
It is <s>hastidantī</s>, <s>nāgadantī</s>, <s>vāruṇī</s>, and <s>gajacirbhaṭā</s>.
It removes diseases of the throat, scrofula, dyspnea, cough, spleen disease, phlegm, and abdominal disease.
It removes an obstructed fetus and conquers skin disease and foul ulcers.
<s>Trāyamāṇā</s> is <s>kṛtatrāṇā</s>, <s>trāyantī</s>, and <s>trāyamāṇakā</s>.
It is <s>baladevā</s>, <s>balabhadrā</s>, <s>vārṣikī</s>, and <s>girisānujā</s>.
<s>Trāyantī</s> is considered to remove phlegm, pitta, blood disorders, abdominal lumps, and fever.
It is hot, pungent and astringent, and destroys puerperal colic.
<s>Yavatiktā</s> and <s>śaṅkhinī</s> are <s>dṛḍhapādā</s> and <s>visarpiṇī</s>.
They are <s>nākulī</s>, <s>akṣapīḍā</s>, <s>netramīlā</s>, and <s>yaśaskarī</s>.
<s>Śatapuṣpā</s> is <s>miśirghoṣā</s>, <s>pītikā</s>, <s>mādhavī</s>, and <s>śiphā</s>.
It is remembered as <s>aticchatrā</s>, <s>avākpuṣpī</s>, <s>śatāhvā</s>, and <s>kāravī</s>.
<s>Śatāhvā</s> is pungent and bitter, unctuous and hot, and conquers phlegm and wind.
It destroys fever, eye disease, and ulcers, and is praised for enema therapy.
The leaf of <s>śatapuṣpā</s> is also said to be aphrodisiac and to conquer blood disorders and abdominal lumps.
It destroys wind, stimulates digestion, promotes breast milk, produces pitta, and gives appetite.
<s>Miśreyā</s> is <s>tālaparṇī</s>, <s>tālapatrī</s>, and likewise <s>miśi</s>.

children.text: śāleyaḥ sa ca śālīno nāmnā śītaśivo mataḥ ||
children.translated_text: It is <s>śāleya</s> and <s>śālīna</s>; by name it is regarded as <s>śītaśiva</s>.
<s>Miśi</s> is bitter, sweet, cooling, aphrodisiac, and conquers piles and wasting.
It is beneficial in injury and emaciation, strengthening, and conquers disorders of wind, pitta, and blood.
<s>Vacā</s> is <s>ugragandhā</s>, <s>golomī</s>, <s>jaṭilogrā</s>, and <s>lomaśā</s>.
Another, white <s>vacā</s>, is intellect-promoting; it is also <s>ṣaḍgranthā</s> and <s>haimavatī</s>.
<s>Vāmanī</s> is pungent, bitter, and hot, and removes pains from wind and phlegm.
It is good for the throat, promotes intellect, kills worms, and removes constipation, distension, and colic.
The two <s>vacā</s>s are pungent, dry and hot, and promote stool and urine.
They stimulate digestion, destroy phlegm and wind, promote intellect and longevity, and digest food.
They kill living parasites, have a strong smell, are light, and conquer diseases of the throat and mouth.
<s>Hapuṣā</s> is <s>vipuṣā</s>, <s>visrā</s>, <s>visragandhā</s>, and <s>atigandhikā</s>.
Another is <s>aśvatthaphalā</s>, <s>kacchūghnī</s>, and <s>dhvāṅkṣanāśinī</s>.
<s>Hapuṣā</s> is pungent, bitter, and hot, heavy, and conquers wind and phlegm.
It destroys piles, abdominal lumps, and colics, together with parasites and abdominal disease.
<s>Viḍaṅga</s> is <s>jantuhantrī</s>, <s>kṛmighnī</s>, and <s>citrataṇḍulā</s>.
It is <s>taṇḍulī</s>, <s>kṛmihā</s>, <s>amoghā</s>, <s>kairalī</s>, and <s>mṛgagāminī</s>.
It is dry and hot, pungent in post-digestive effect, light, and removes wind and phlegm.
Slightly bitter, <s>viḍaṅga</s> destroys poisons and kills worms.
<s>Kuṭaja</s> is <s>kauṭaja</s>, <s>kauṭa</s>, <s>vatsaka</s>, and <s>girimallikā</s>.
It is <s>kaliṅga</s>, <s>mallikāpuṣpa</s>, <s>indravṛkṣa</s>, and then <s>vṛkṣaka</s>.
<s>Kuṭaja</s> is pungent, bitter, astringent, dry, and cooling.
It destroys skin disease, diarrhea, pitta, blood disorders, and diseases arising in the anus.
Its fruits are <s>indrayava</s>, called <s>śakrāhvā</s> and <s>kaliṅgaka</s>.
They are also called <s>vatsakabīja</s> and likewise <s>bhadrayava</s>.
<s>Śakrāhvā</s>s are pungent, bitter, hot, destroy the three doṣas, and stimulate digestion.
They destroy bleeding piles and diarrhea, and likewise colic and vomiting.
<s>Yavakṣāra</s> is remembered as <s>pākya</s>, <s>yavaja</s>, and <s>yavaśūkaja</s>.
It is <s>yavāhva</s>, <s>śūkaja</s>, <s>yavya</s>, <s>yāvaśūka</s>, and <s>yavāgraja</s>.
<s>Yavakṣāra</s> is pungent and hot, and conquers phlegm, wind, abdominal disease, and pain.
It removes undigested-food colic, stones, urinary difficulty, poison, and doṣa disorders, and is flowing in action.
It is hot, drying, sharp, digestive-kindling, and conquers phlegm and wind.
It vitiates pitta and blood, is good for the heart, and is called the alkali born from barley.
Another alkali is <s>svarjikākṣāra</s>; it is <s>svarjikā</s> and <s>suvarcikā</s>.

children.text: suvarcikaḥ suvarco'tha sukhavarcaḥ sa eva ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Suvarcika</s>, <s>suvarcas</s>, and <s>sukhavarcas</s> are the same substance.
<s>Svarjikā</s> is hot, pungent, and alkaline in taste; it conquers wind and phlegm.
It destroys abdominal lumps, distension, and worms, and removes fat and abdominal disease.
<s>Ṭaṅkaṇa</s> and <s>ṭaṅkaṇakṣāra</s> arise from the juice of <s>mālatī</s>.
It is melting and liquefying, and purifies metals.
<s>Ṭaṅkaṇakṣāra</s> is said to be pungent and hot, and to destroy phlegm.
It also counters poisons beginning with fixed poisons, and removes cough and dyspnea.
It dries, removes wind, destroys phlegm, and corrupts pitta.
<s>Ṭaṅkaṇakṣāra</s> is called sharp and kindling to the digestive fire.

children.text: saindhavaṃ sindhu sindhūtthaṃ nādeyaṃ sindhujaṃ śivam
children.translated_text: <s>Saindhava</s> is called <s>sindhu</s>, <s>sindhūttha</s>, <s>nādeya</s>, <s>sindhuja</s>, and <s>śiva</s>.
It is also called pure, cooling and wholesome, <s>maṇimantha</s>, and stony in nature.

children.text: saindhavaṃ śiśiraṃ snigdhaṃ laghu svādu tridoṣajit
children.translated_text: <s>Saindhava</s> is cooling, unctuous, light, sweet, and conquers the three doṣas.
It is good for the heart, destroys diseases of the heart and eyes, and removes lack of appetite caused by wounds.
<s>Saindhava</s> is sweet, beneficial for the eyes, aphrodisiac, appetizing, and digestive-fire-kindling.
It is non-burning, removes constipation, gives comfort, and conquers the three doṣas.
<s>Viḍa</s> is called artificial, <s>dhūrta</s>, alkaline, Dravidian, and demonic.
Its names are <s>supākya</s>, <s>khaṇḍalavaṇa</s>, and <s>kṛtaka</s>.
Containing alkali, it kindles digestion and destroys colic, heart disease, and phlegm.
<s>Viḍa</s> is appetizing, sharp, hot, and promotes the downward movement of wind.
<s>Akṣa</s> is called <s>sauvarcala</s>, <s>rucaka</s>, and <s>hṛdyagandhaka</s>.
It is remembered as <s>tilaka</s>, black salt, and instant salt.

children.text: laghu sauvarcalaṃ pāke vīryoṣṇaṃ viśadaṃ kaṭu
children.translated_text: <s>Sauvarcala</s> is light, hot in post-digestive effect and potency, clear, and pungent.
It removes abdominal lumps, colic, and constipation; it is heart-pleasing, fragrant, and appetizing.
<s>Audbhida</s> is <s>pāṃśulavaṇa</s>, <s>romaka</s>, <s>vasuka</s>, and <s>vasu</s>.
It is also <s>ūṣara</s>, <s>pāṃsavakṣāra</s>, <s>aurva</s>, and of all qualities.
It is light, sharp, hot, moistening, subtle, and promotes the downward movement of wind.
One should know <s>audbhida</s> salt as somewhat bitter, pungent, and alkaline.

children.text: sāmudralavaṇaṃ prāhuḥ kṣāraṃ ca śiśiraṃ tathā
children.translated_text: They call it sea salt, also alkaline and cooling.
It is born from the sea, born from the ocean, and produced from the salty ocean.
Sea salt is not excessively hot in post-digestive effect and is non-burning.
It is breaking, slightly unctuous, removes colic, and is not very pitta-provoking.
<s>Hiṅgu</s> is <s>rāmaṭha</s>, very fierce, killer of creatures, and destroyer of harmful beings.
It is <s>agūḍhagandha</s>, <s>bāhlīka</s>, digestive, and used for fumigating soups.

children.text: hiṅgūṣṇaṃ kaṭukaṃ hṛdyaṃ saraṃ vātakaphau kṛmīn
children.translated_text: <s>Hiṅgu</s> is hot, pungent, heart-pleasing, flowing, and destroys wind, phlegm, and worms.
It destroys abdominal lumps, abdominal disease, distension, obstruction, colic, and heart ailments.

children.text: hiṅgupattrī tu kavarī pṛthvīkā pṛthulā pṛthuḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Hiṅgupattrī</s> is <s>kavarī</s>, <s>pṛthvīkā</s>, <s>pṛthulā</s>, and <s>pṛthu</s>.
It is <s>bāṣpikā</s>, <s>dīrghikā</s>, <s>tanvī</s>, <s>bilvikā</s>, and <s>dārupattrikā</s>.
<s>Bāṣpikā</s> is pungent, sharp, hot, good for the heart, and removes wind and phlegm.
It removes worms, spleen disease, constipation, piles, abdominal lumps, and pain in the heart and bladder.

children.text: nāḍīhiṅgu palāśākhyā jantukā rāmaṭhī ca sā
children.translated_text: <s>Nāḍīhiṅgu</s> is known as <s>palāśā</s>, <s>jantukā</s>, and <s>rāmaṭhī</s>.
It is <s>vaṃśapattrī</s>, <s>veṇupattrī</s>, <s>piṇḍā</s>, and <s>hiṅguśivāṭikā</s>.
<s>Nāḍīhiṅgu</s> is pungent and hot, and greatly calms phlegm and wind.
It destroys obstruction, constipation, and disorders from undigested matter, and is supremely digestive-fire-kindling.

children.text: tumburuḥ saurabhaḥ sauro vanajaḥ sānujo dvijaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Tumburu</s> is <s>saurabha</s>, <s>saura</s>, forest-born, <s>sānuja</s>, and <s>dvija</s>.
It has sharp bark, sharp fruit, and sharp leaves, and is called <s>mahāmuni</s>.
<s>Tumburu</s> is pungent, sharp, hot, and conquers phlegm, wind, and colic.
It destroys convulsive disorders, abdominal disease, distension, and worms, and kindles the digestive fire.

children.text: sūkṣmailā drāviḍī tutthā koraṅgī bahulā truṭiḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Sūkṣmailā</s> is <s>drāviḍī</s>, <s>tutthā</s>, <s>koraṅgī</s>, <s>bahulā</s>, and <s>truṭi</s>.

children.text: elā kapotavarṇā ca candrabālā ca niṣkuṭī ||
children.translated_text: It is <s>elā</s>, pigeon-colored, <s>candrabālā</s>, and <s>niṣkuṭī</s>.
<s>Candana</s> is sandalwood, essence of fragrance, very valuable, and white sandalwood.
It is <s>bhadraśrī</s>, born in Malaya, <s>gośīrṣa</s>, and <s>tilaparṇaka</s>.
<s>Śrīkhaṇḍa</s> is cooling, sweet, bitter, and destroys pitta.
It clarifies the blood, is aphrodisiac, and removes internal burning.
It destroys pitta, blood disorders, poison, thirst, burning, and worms; it is heavy and drying.
All sandalwood is somewhat bitter and sweet; sandalwood is supremely cooling.
Red sandalwood is another kind, called red, yellow sandalwood,
<s>raktasāra</s>, <s>tāmrasāra</s>, and it is designated as lesser sandalwood.
They also say red sandalwood repels harmful beings, and is bitter and cooling.
It removes excess blood and destroys very severe aggravation of pitta.
<s>Kucandana</s> is <s>pataṅga</s>, red wood, and <s>suraṅgaka</s>.
It is <s>pattrāṅga</s>, <s>paṭṭarāga</s>, and also <s>paṭṭarañjana</s>.
It is sweet in post-digestive taste, cooling, phlegm-producing, and not very pitta-provoking.
<s>Kucandana</s> is bitter, fragrant, and heals wounds.
<s>Kālīyaka</s> is yellow, and also dear to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.
It is born in Malaya, yellow wood, and the fourth, yellow sandalwood.
<s>Kālīyaka</s> is rich in purity, cooling, and conquers blood-pitta.
Next, <s>barbarika</s> is white, odorless, and born in the barbarian land.
It destroys pitta, blood disorders, phlegm, burning, and worms; it is heavy and drying.
All these are equal in taste and likewise in potency.

children.text: gandhena tu viśeṣaḥ syāt pūrvaṃ śreṣṭhatamaṃ guṇaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: But there is a difference in fragrance; the earlier one is best in qualities.
<s>Kuṅkuma</s> is <s>rudhira</s>, red, <s>asṛgasra</s>, and yellowish.

children.text: kāśmīraṃ cāru bāhlīkaṃ saṃkocaṃ piśunaṃ varam ||
children.translated_text: It is <s>kāśmīra</s>, beautiful, <s>bāhlīka</s>, <s>saṃkoca</s>, <s>piśuna</s>, and excellent.
<s>Kuṅkuma</s> is pungent, bitter, hot, and conquers phlegm and wind.
It removes wounds, eye disease, head disease, and poison, and produces bodily beauty.
<s>Uśīra</s> is also <s>amṛṇāla</s>, fearless, and of even fragrance.
It is <s>raṇapriya</s>, <s>vīrataru</s>, <s>vīra</s>, and <s>vīraṇamūlaka</s>.

children.text: uśīraṃ śītalaṃ tiktaṃ dāhakāntiharaṃ ca tat
children.translated_text: <s>Uśīra</s> is cooling, bitter, and removes burning and loss of complexion.
When properly used, it removes wind, fever, thirst, and urinary disorder, and stops bleeding.
<s>Uśīra</s> removes the bad odor of sweat and pitta; it is unctuous and bitter.

children.text: priyaṅguḥ priyavallī ca phalinī kaṅgunī priyā
children.translated_text: <s>Priyaṅgu</s> is <s>priyavallī</s>, <s>phalinī</s>, <s>kaṅgunī</s>, and <s>priyā</s>.
It is <s>vṛttā</s>, <s>govandanī</s>, <s>śyāmā</s>, <s>kārambhā</s>, and <s>varṇabhedanī</s>.
<s>Priyaṅgu</s> is cooling and bitter, and destroys fainting and burning.
It removes fever and vomiting, and clarifies agitated blood.
<s>Tūṇi</s> is <s>tūṇīkaṇa</s>, <s>pītatūṇika</s>, and also <s>kanaka</s>.
It is <s>kuṭheraka</s>, <s>kāntalaka</s>, <s>nandivṛkṣa</s>, and then <s>nandika</s>.
<s>Tūṇī</s> removes the three doṣas, is aphrodisiac, and removes itching, skin disease, and wounds.
It removes scrofulous swellings and cuts away sannipāta, the combined disorder of the doṣas.

children.text: rocanā piṅgalā piṅgā medhyā gaurī ca gomatī
children.translated_text: <s>Rocanā</s> is <s>piṅgalā</s>, <s>piṅgā</s>, <s>medhyā</s>, <s>gaurī</s>, and <s>gomatī</s>.
It is auspicious, venerable, foremost, purifying, beautiful, and <s>ruci</s>.
<s>Rocanā</s> is digestive and cooling; it conquers poison and diseases of the eyes.
It brings good fortune and destroys faults caused by spirits and grahas.

children.text: turuṣko yāvanaḥ kalkaḥ piṇyākaḥ piṇḍitaḥ kapiḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Turuṣka</s> is <s>yāvana</s>, <s>kalka</s>, <s>piṇyāka</s>, <s>piṇḍita</s>, and <s>kapi</s>.
It is <s>kapija</s>, artificial, smoky, smoke-colored, and <s>silhaka</s>.
It is fragrant, artificial, properly prepared, and <s>piṇḍaka</s>.
It is known as <s>kapitaila</s>, and also by the name <s>piṅgala</s>.
<s>Turuṣka</s> is pungent, bitter, hot, unctuous, and conquers wind and phlegm.
It is sweet, pungent in digestion, fragrant, and dear to the gods.
<s>Agaru</s> is excellent, <s>loha</s>, worm-eaten, and <s>anāryaka</s>.
It is black <s>agaru</s>, sweet <s>agaru</s>, <s>yogaja</s>, and <s>viśvarūpaka</s>.
<s>Agaru</s> is pungent, bitter, hot, and unctuous; it removes wind and phlegm.
It removes diseases of the ears and eyes, is auspicious, and is supreme for removing skin disease.

children.text: kāleyakaṃ sasāraṃ ca pītavarṇaṃ ca śabdataḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Kāleyaka</s>, also called <s>sasāra</s>, is said to be yellow in color.
It improves complexion and is indeed light sandalwood.
<s>Kastūrikā</s> is <s>mṛgamada</s>, <s>mṛganābhi</s>, and born from the deer's testicle.
It is <s>mārjārī</s>, foremost in piercing power, <s>madanī</s>, and <s>gandhacelikā</s>.
<s>Kastūrikā</s> is bitter and pungent in taste, and removes phlegm and wind.
It counteracts poison, pacifies doṣas, and is excellent for removing dryness of the mouth.
<s>Karpūra</s> is cooling dust, cool cloud, crystal, and snow.
It is moon, frost, cold dew, hare-marked moon, moon, and snowy sand.

children.text: karpūraṃ kaṭutiktaṃ ca madhuraṃ śiśiraṃ viduḥ
children.translated_text: They know <s>karpūra</s> as pungent, bitter, sweet, and cold.
It removes thirst, fat, poison, and doṣas, benefits the eyes, and causes intoxication.
<s>Jātipatrī</s> is <s>jātikośā</s> and also <s>sumanaḥpattrikā</s>.
It is also <s>mālatīpattrikā</s>, and is said to destroy impurity.
<s>Jātipatrī</s> is pungent and hot, fragrant, and destroys phlegm.
It removes bad odor of the mouth, improves complexion, removes poison, and gives bodily calm.
<s>Jātīphala</s> is <s>jātisasya</s>, <s>śālūka</s>, and <s>mālatīphala</s>.
It is <s>madaśauṇḍa</s>, <s>jātiśṛṅga</s>, <s>puṭa</s>, and the fragrant fruit.
<s>Jātīphala</s> is astringent, hot, and pungent; it conquers throat disease and pain.
It removes wind, diarrhea, and urinary disorder, is light, aphrodisiac, and kindles digestion.
<s>Kaṅkolaka</s> is <s>kṛtaphala</s>, <s>kolaka</s>, and the pungent fruit.
It is <s>cūrṇa</s>, <s>kandaphala</s>, island pepper, and esteemed by <s>Mādhava</s>.
<s>Kaṅkola</s> is pungent, bitter, and hot, and removes bad taste in the mouth.
It removes numbness of the mouth, is pleasing to the taste, and is supreme for removing wind and phlegm.
<s>Pūgaphala</s> is <s>udvega</s>; it is remembered as laxative and as <s>ghoṇṭāphala</s>.

children.text: cikkaṇaṃ cikkaṇā cikkā guvākaḥ khapuraṃ ca tat ||
children.translated_text: It is <s>cikkaṇa</s>, <s>cikkaṇā</s>, <s>cikkā</s>, <s>guvāka</s>, and <s>khapura</s>.

children.text: bhedi saṃmohakṛt pūgaṃ kaṣāyaṃ svādu rocanam
children.translated_text: <s>Pūga</s> is purgative and stupefying, astringent, sweet, and appetizing.
It removes phlegm and pitta, is dry, and removes moisture and dirt from the mouth.
<s>Lavaṅga</s> is <s>devakusuma</s>, <s>bhṛṅgāra</s>, <s>śikhara</s>, and <s>lava</s>.
It is divine, sandal-flower, <s>śrīpuṣpa</s>, and water-born.
The flower of <s>lavaṅga</s> is pleasant to the heart, cooling, and destroys pitta.
It benefits the eyes, removes poison, is aphrodisiac and auspicious, and removes diseases of the head.
<s>Nalikā</s> is <s>vidrumalatā</s>, <s>kapotacaraṇā</s>, and <s>nalī</s>.

children.text: suṣirā dhamanī śūnyā nirmathyā nartakī naṭā ||
children.translated_text: It is hollow, tubular, empty, to be churned, dancer, and actor.
<s>Nalikā</s> removes bleeding disorders, benefits the eyes, and destroys poison.

children.text: nalikā vātalā tiktā gurvī ca madhurā himā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Nalikā</s> produces wind, and is bitter, heavy, sweet, and cold.

children.text: māṃsī kṛṣṇajaṭā hiṃsrā naladā jaṭilā miśī
children.translated_text: <s>Māṃsī</s> is <s>kṛṣṇajaṭā</s>, <s>hiṃsrā</s>, <s>naladā</s>, <s>jaṭilā</s>, and <s>miśī</s>.

children.text: jaṭā ca piśitā peśī kravyādī ca tapasvinī ||
children.translated_text: It is <s>jaṭā</s>, <s>piśitā</s>, <s>peśī</s>, flesh-eater, and ascetic.
<s>Māṃsī</s> is sweet and astringent, and destroys phlegm, pitta, and blood disorders.
It removes poison and wind, strengthens the heart, benefits the skin, and clarifies beauty.

children.text: dvitīyā gandhamāṃsī syāt keśī bhūtajaṭā smṛtā
children.translated_text: The second kind is <s>gandhamāṃsī</s>; it is remembered as <s>keśī</s> and <s>bhūtajaṭā</s>.

children.text: piśācī pūtanā keśī bhūtakeśī ca lomaśā ||
children.translated_text: It is <s>piśācī</s>, <s>pūtanā</s>, <s>keśī</s>, <s>bhūtakeśī</s>, and <s>lomaśā</s>.
The two <s>māṃsī</s>s are astringent, improve complexion, and remove pitta and phlegm.

children.text: rakṣoghnaṃ ca sugandhi syād vātaghnaṃ keśyamuttamam ||
children.translated_text: They destroy demons, are fragrant, remove wind, and are excellent for the hair.
<s>Kuṣṭha</s> is disease, medicine, ailment, blue lotus, <s>pākala</s>, and pain.
It is <s>vāpya</s>, water-born, <s>rāma</s>, <s>kaubera</s>, and <s>pāribhadraka</s>.
<s>Kuṣṭha</s> is pungent, hot, and bitter; it conquers phlegm, wind, and blood disorders.
It destroys the three doṣas, poison, itching, and skin diseases.

children.text: reṇukā rājaputrī ca nandinī kapilā dvijā
children.translated_text: <s>Reṇukā</s> is <s>rājaputrī</s>, <s>nandinī</s>, <s>kapilā</s>, and twice-born.
It is remembered as <s>kapilolā</s>, <s>pāṇḍuputrī</s>, <s>kauntī</s>, and <s>hareṇukā</s>.
<s>Reṇukā</s> is extremely cooling and destroys thirst and itching.
When applied, it removes poison and uproots burning and weakness.

children.text: tagaraṃ kuṭilaṃ vakraṃ dīnaṃ jihmaṃ nataṃ śaṭham
children.translated_text: <s>Tagara</s> is crooked, bent, low, oblique, bowed, and deceitful.
It is <s>kālānusārya</s>, not straight, curled, <s>nahuṣa</s>, and king.
<s>Tagara</s> is astringent, hot, unctuous, and drives away all three doṣas.
It removes disorders of the eyes and head, poison and doṣa afflictions, and destroys spirit-seizure and epilepsy.
<s>Pariplava</s>, <s>plava</s>, wild, and <s>gopuṭa</s> are <s>kuṭannaṭa</s>.
It is white-flowered, <s>dāśapura</s>, <s>gonarda</s>, and old-flowered.
<s>Pariplava</s> is fragrant; it conquers sweat, dirt, and itching.
It also conquers wind and phlegm, is good for the intellect, and bestows beauty.

children.text: nakhaḥ kararuhaḥ śilpī karajo'tha khuraḥ śaphaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Nakha</s> is nail-born, an artisan, and hand-born; then <s>khura</s> and <s>śapha</s>.
It is shell, conch, moving, encased, jaw, elephant-jaw, and strong.

children.text: nakhaṃ kaṭukamuṣṇaṃ ca viṣaṃ hanti prayojitam
children.translated_text: <s>Nakha</s> is pungent and hot; when used, it destroys poison.
It certainly subdues skin diseases and at once breaks up phlegm.
Another <s>nakha</s> is <s>vyāghranakha</s>; it is considered <s>puṭa</s> and the tiger's weapon.
It is blood, tiger's paw, foot, standing firm, and diamond-maker.
<s>Vyāghranakha</s> is bitter, hot, and astringent; it conquers phlegm and wind.
It destroys itching, skin disease, and wounds, improves complexion, and is supreme in giving fragrance.
<s>Spṛkkā</s> is <s>sṛgbrāhmaṇī</s>, goddess, <s>mālālī</s>, and is considered <s>koṭikā</s>.
It is <s>pañcamuṣṭi</s>, daughter of the gods, cast-off garland, slanderous woman, and bride.

children.text: spṛkkā śītā sugandhā syāt tṛṣṇāṃ muṣṇāti yojitā
children.translated_text: <s>Spṛkkā</s> is cooling and fragrant; when applied it steals away thirst.
It destroys poison and certainly removes burning that arises in the body.
<s>Spṛkkā</s> is fragrant, destroys skin disease, and removes bad odor and sweating.

children.text: bolaṃ gandharasaṃ piṇḍaṃ nirlohaṃ barbaraṃ rasam
children.translated_text: <s>Bola</s> is fragrant resin, lump, ironless, barbarian, and resin.

children.text: gopakaṃ nālikaṃ pauraṃ viṣaṃ gandharasaṃ viduḥ ||
children.translated_text: They know <s>gopaka</s>, <s>nālika</s>, <s>paura</s>, and poison as <s>gandharasa</s>.

children.text: bolaṃ tiktaṃ himaṃ raktamudriktaṃ hanti yogataḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Bola</s> is bitter and cold; when properly used it destroys aggravated blood.
It destroys diseases of phlegm and pitta and removes pains such as pradarā.

children.text: damanaḥ pāṇḍurāgaḥ syāt dāntaḥ gandhotkaṭo muniḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Damana</s> is pale-colored, tamed, strongly fragrant, and sage.
It is white lotus, Brahmā's matted hair, ascetic, and son of a sage.
<s>Damana</s> is bitter in taste, destroys poison, and removes disorders caused by spirits.
It is remembered as pacifying the three doṣas, pleasing to the heart, and removing itching and skin disease.
Another <s>damana</s> is <s>dama</s>, calm, sage, and endowed with self-restraint.
It is devoted to forbearance and tranquility, virtuous, good, and pleasantly fragrant.
<s>Murā</s> is fragrant, demonic, rich in fragrance, and wearing a garland of scent.

children.text: surabhir bhūrigandhā ca kuṭī gandhakuṭī smṛtā ||
children.translated_text: It is fragrant, very fragrant, hut, and is remembered as fragrance-hut.
<s>Murā</s> is extremely cooling, bitter, and sweetly fragrant.
It reduces masses of wounds and brings about the pacification of pitta.
<s>Sthauṇeyaka</s> is peacock-crested, parrot-flowered, and parrot-leaved.
It is split-eared, parrot-plumed, green, and with fallen hair.
<s>Sthauṇeya</s> destroys phlegm and wind, is fragrant, and is pungent and bitter.
It pacifies provoked pitta and increases strength and nourishment.
<s>Coraka</s> is suspicious, fierce, bad-leaved, secure, and enemy.
It is group-laughter, irascible, gambler, and fruit-thief.
<s>Coraka</s> is extremely cooling and brings an end to poison and blood disorders.
When used, it destroys skin disease, itching, wounds, and doṣas at once.
<s>Coraka</s> is also intensely fragrant and bitter, and conquers worms and wind.
<s>Śaileya</s> is grey-haired, old, aged, and <s>kālānusāryaka</s>.
It is elderly, rock-lichen, rock-flower, and rock-born.
<s>Śaileyaka</s> is said to be cold, conquer burning, and destroy poison.
It removes blood disorders and is remembered as uprooting itching.
<s>Śaileya</s> is bitter, cooling, fragrant, and conquers phlegm and pitta.
It destroys burning, thirst, vomiting, dyspnea, wounds, and doṣa disorders.
<s>Elavāluka</s> is <s>ālūka</s>, <s>vāluka</s>, and <s>harivāluka</s>.
<s>Elvāluka</s> is <s>kapittha</s>, bad-colored, spreading, and firm.
<s>Elavālu</s> is fragrant and is proclaimed to be extremely cooling.
It destroys poison and brings an end to very severe itching, skin disease, and wounds.

children.text: saralaḥ pūtikāṣṭhaṃ ca cīḍā pūtidrumo mataḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Sarala</s> is foul-smelling wood, <s>cīḍā</s>, and is considered the foul-smelling tree.
It is lamp-tree, unctuous wood, and is called pepper-leaved.
<s>Sarala</s> is unctuous, bitter, and hot, and destroys phlegm and wind.
It brings an end to mouth-salivation, loss of voice, eye disease, and wounds.
<s>Saptaparṇa</s> is shell-leaved, umbrella-leaved, and good-leaved.
It is seven-leaved, hidden-flowered, and also silk-cotton-leaved.
It pacifies the three doṣas, is pleasing to the heart, fragrant, digestive, and fluid-moving.
<s>Śālmalipattraka</s> destroys colic, abdominal tumors, worms, and skin disease.

children.text: lākṣā palaṅkaṣā raktā dīptiśca kṛmijā jatu
children.translated_text: <s>Lākṣā</s> is <s>palaṅkaṣā</s>, red, brilliance, and lac produced by insects.
It is hundred-slayer, mother of dye, tree-disease, and red lac.
<s>Lākṣā</s> is bitter and astringent, unctuous, and removes blood and pitta disorders.
It destroys worms, phlegm, and wounds, and removes affliction from spirits and fever.
<s>Tāmalakyajaṭā</s> is <s>tālī</s>, while <s>tamālī</s> is <s>tamālinī</s>.
It is <s>vitunnā</s>, <s>bhūmyāmalakī</s>, <s>bhūdhātrī</s>, and also <s>bhvāmalakī</s>.

children.text: bhūdhātrī madhurā tiktā vīryataḥ śiśirā smṛtā
children.translated_text: <s>Bhūdhātrī</s> is sweet and bitter, and is remembered as cooling in potency.
It destroys pitta, removes phlegm and blood disorders, and eliminates disorders of sight and burning.
<s>Lāmajjaka</s> is good-stalked, without lotus-fiber, <s>lava</s>, and light.
It is brick-path, swift, long-rooted, and water-dwelling.
<s>Lāmajjaka</s> is bitter and is considered extremely cold.
It produces pacification of pitta and destroys poison and blood disorders.
<s>Padmaka</s> is <s>malaya</s>, beautiful, yellow-red, and divine in origin.
It is very bright, cooling in potency, and colored like a pāṭalā flower.
<s>Padmaka</s> is cooling, unctuous, astringent, and removes blood-pitta disorders.
It is said to stabilize pregnancy and to remove fever, vomiting, and poison.
It pacifies delusion, burning, fever, confusion, skin disease, and eruptions.
<s>Dhātakī</s> is copper-flowered, elephantine, and dwelling in liquor.

children.text: pārvatīyā subhikṣā ca vahnipuṣpā ca śabditā ||
children.translated_text: It is called <s>pārvatīyā</s>, <s>subhikṣā</s>, and <s>vahnipuṣpā</s>.
<s>Dhātakī</s> is pungent and hot, intoxicating, and destroys poison.
It removes diarrhea, stabilizes pregnancy, and reduces worms and blood disorders.
<s>Prapauṇḍarīka</s> benefits the eyes; it is <s>puṇḍarya</s> and <s>puṇḍarīyaka</s>.
It is white-flowered, fine-flowered, <s>śrīpuṣpa</s>, and <s>sānujānuja</s>.
<s>Prapauṇḍarīka</s> is sweet, astringent, bitter, and cool.
It removes pitta, blood disorders, and wounds, and takes away fever, burning, and thirst.

children.text: karcūro gandhamūlaśca drāviḍaṃ kārśa eva ca
children.translated_text: <s>Karcūra</s> is <s>gandhamūla</s>, <s>drāviḍa</s>, and <s>kārśa</s>.
It is foremost among piercing substances, rare, and by some accepted as <s>śaṭī</s>.
<s>Karcūra</s> is pungent, bitter, hot, appetizing, and conquers wind and phlegm.
It kindles digestion and pacifies spleen disease, abdominal lumps, and piles; it overcomes skin disease and cough.
<s>Manaḥśilā</s> is <s>manoguptā</s>, <s>manohvā</s>, <s>kunaṭī</s>, and <s>śilā</s>.

children.text: manojñā nāgajihvā ca golā nepālikā kalā ||
children.translated_text: It is <s>manojñā</s>, <s>nāgajihvā</s>, <s>golā</s>, <s>nepālikā</s>, and <s>kalā</s>.
<s>Manaḥśilā</s> is pungent, bitter, hot, and destructive of poison.
By applications, forehead-marks, and the like, it removes fear from spirit-possession.
<s>Sindūra</s> is <s>raktareṇu</s>, <s>nāgagarbha</s>, and <s>nāgaja</s>.
It is an ornament of adornment, splendid, and a decoration for the spring festival.
<s>Sindūra</s> is hot and pungent, and removes poison and corrupted wounds.
It is supreme for removing skin disorders, skin disease, erysipelas, and chronic fever.
In the great mountains there is a smaller essence situated inside stone.
When dried and red, it is designated by the name <s>girisindūra</s>.
<s>Girisindūra</s> is said to pacify the three doṣas, to be purgative, to bind mercury, and to kindle digestion.
It produces firmness of the body and metals, and benefits the eyes.
<s>Saurāṣṭrī</s> is <s>amṛtāsaṅgā</s>, <s>kāṅkṣī</s>, <s>kākṣī</s>, and born in <s>Surāṣṭra</s>.

children.text: ajitā tuvarī stutyā mṛtsā mṛtsnā mṛtālakam ||
children.translated_text: It is <s>ajitā</s>, <s>tuvarī</s>, praised, clay, earth, and <s>mṛtālaka</s>.

children.text: kāṅkṣī kaṭukaṣāyā syāt keśyā caiva viṣāpahā
children.translated_text: <s>Kāṅkṣī</s> is pungent and astringent; it is good for the hair and removes poison.
It destroys itching, erysipelas, and leucoderma, and heals wounds.
<s>Gandhaka</s> is <s>gandhapāṣāṇa</s>, <s>lelīta</s>, and <s>gandhamādana</s>.
It is foul-smelling, <s>balivatsā</s>, fragrant stone, destructive of metals, and strong.
<s>Gandhaka</s> is pungent, bitter, hot, intensely odorous, and very odor-producing.
It destroys poison, skin disease, itching, scabies, and skin disorders.
<s>Vaṭasaugandhika</s>, <s>gandha</s>, <s>gandhaka</s>, and <s>gandhamādana</s>,
as well as <s>lelīna</s>, <s>gandhapāṣāṇa</s>, <s>lelīta</s>, and <s>nikṛntana</s>, are its names.
It destroys skin disorders, skin disease, erysipelas, metals, and mercury.
This <s>gandhaka</s> is regarded as an excellent rasāyana, pungent and hot.
<s>Mācikā</s> is the renowned <s>ambaṣṭhā</s>, and also <s>ambā</s>, <s>ambālikā</s>, and <s>ambikā</s>.

children.text: ambaṣṭhakā kaṣāyā ca sā proktā mukhavācikā ||
children.translated_text: It is <s>ambaṣṭhakā</s>, astringent, and is called <s>mukhavācikā</s>.

children.text: ambikā tu rase tiktā tathoṣṇā kaphanāśanī
children.translated_text: <s>Ambikā</s> is bitter in taste, hot, and destructive of phlegm.
It is remembered as removing piles and as opposing the arising of swelling.
<s>Sikthaka</s> is <s>madhuka</s>, <s>siktha</s>, beeswax, and produced from honey.
It is <s>madhuśeṣa</s>, <s>madanaka</s>, honey-born, and dependent on bees.
<s>Sikthaka</s> is unctuous and sweet, destroys spirits, and mends broken joints.
It removes erysipelas, itching, and the like, and is excellent for healing wounds.
It is purgative, slimy, sweet, mild, and conquers skin disease and gouty blood disorder.
<s>Rāla</s> is <s>sarjarasa</s>, <s>śāla</s>, <s>kṣaṇa</s>, and born from <s>kalakala</s>.
It is <s>lalana</s>, resin of the <s>śāla</s>, incense of yakṣas, and beloved of fire.
<s>Rāla</s> is sweet, astringent, hot, styptic, and wound-healing.
For it destroys poison and spirits and joins broken bones.
<s>Kāsīsa</s> is <s>dhātukāsīsa</s>, <s>kesara</s>, and <s>taptalomaśa</s>.
<s>Kāsīsa</s> is astringent, hot, sour, and conquers wind and phlegm.
It removes poison, eye pain, leucoderma, skin disease, and wounds as well.
The second is <s>puṣpakāsīsa</s>, also <s>vatsaka</s> and <s>malīmasa</s>.
It is short, useful as eye medicine, clarifying, and blue clay.
<s>Puṣpādikāsīsa</s> is highly praised, warm, astringent, sour, and exceedingly beneficial for the eyes.
It destroys poison, fire-like burning, phlegmatic disease, wounds, leucoderma, and wasting, and it is a coloring for the hair.
<s>Guggulu</s> is <s>kālaniryāsa</s>, <s>jaṭāyu</s>, <s>kauśika</s>, and <s>pura</s>.
It is <s>naktaṃcara</s>, <s>śivā</s>, <s>durgā</s>, <s>mahiṣākṣa</s>, and <s>palaṃkaṣa</s>.
