<s>Guggulu</s> is said to be slimy, pungent, bitter, and astringent.

children.text: varṇyaḥ svaryo laghuḥ sūkṣmo rūkṣo vātabalāsajit ||
children.translated_text: It improves complexion and voice, is light, subtle, dry, and conquers wind and phlegm.
<s>Kunduru</s> is <s>kunduruka</s>, <s>śikharī</s>, and <s>kundragopura</s>.
It is <s>sukundra</s>, sharp-scented, <s>pālinda</s>, fearsome, and strong.
<s>Kunduru</s> is pungent and bitter, and removes wind, phlegm, and impurities.
In drinking and in application it is cooling, and it pacifies disorders of excessive discharge.
<s>Śrīveṣṭaka</s> is the incense-tree, milk-headed, and rough-tree.
It is <s>śrīvāsa</s>, <s>pāyasa</s>, <s>śryāhva</s>, milk-flowing, and curd.
<s>Śrīveṣṭa</s> is sweet and bitter, astringent, and wound-healing.
It removes disorders born of phlegm, pitta, and blood, destroys seizures, and removes diseases of the head.

children.text: śallakī vallakī hlādā surabhiḥ susravā ca sā
children.translated_text: <s>Śallakī</s> is <s>vallakī</s>, <s>hlādā</s>, fragrant, and well-flowing.
It is <s>aśvamūtrī</s>, <s>kundurukī</s>, elephant-food, and <s>maheraṇā</s>.
<s>Śallakī</s> is said to be astringent and extremely cooling in potency.
It removes phlegm and is regarded as pacifying the aggravation of pitta.
Next, <s>Kampillaka</s> is red-limbed, <s>recī</s>, and <s>recanaka</s>.
It is <s>rañjana</s>, <s>lohitāṅga</s>, <s>kampilla</s>, and red powder.
<s>Kampillaka</s> is purgative, pungent, hot, and destructive of wounds.
It destroys abdominal lumps, abdominal disease, constipation, distension, phlegm, and worms.
<s>Kaṅkuṣṭha</s> is <s>kālakuṣṭha</s>, <s>viraṅga</s>, and lord of dyes.
It is purgative, bristling, wasting, cleansing, and <s>kālapālaka</s>.
<s>Kaṅkuṣṭha</s> is proclaimed to be bitter and pungent, and hot in potency.
It removes abdominal tumors, intestinal obstruction, and pain; it colors rasa preparations and removes wounds.
<s>Bhallātaka</s> is remembered as <s>aruṣka</s>, burner, heater, and fire-like.
It is <s>aruṣkara</s>, heroic tree, <s>bhallāta</s>, fire-faced, and bow.
<s>Bhallāta</s> is pungent, bitter, hot, sweet, and destroys worms.
It destroys abdominal tumors, piles, grahaṇī disorders, skin diseases, and illnesses of wind and phlegm.
<s>Tuttha</s> is <s>karparikātuttha</s>, and also <s>amṛtāsaṅga</s>.
Another <s>tutthaka</s> is <s>mayūragrīvaka</s> and <s>śitikaṇṭha</s>.
The second is <s>karparītuttha</s>, and likewise <s>karparītutthaka</s>.
That <s>tuttha</s>, like nectar, should make the eyes clear.
<s>Tutthaka</s> removes diseases of sight, is cooling, and destroys white leprosy.
The wise say that it is excellent for calming the force of poison.
<s>Hemamākṣika</s> is <s>āvarta</s>, <s>tāpīja</s>, and <s>dhātumākṣika</s>.

children.text: tāpyaṃ ca mākṣikaṃ dhātu madhudhātu vinirdiśet ||
children.translated_text: One should designate <s>tāpya</s>, <s>mākṣika</s>, mineral, and honey-mineral as the same.
<s>Mākṣika</s> is pungent, bitter, hot, and an unsurpassed rejuvenative.
It removes bladder disease and destroys piles, swelling, abdominal disease, and wasting.
It pacifies the three doṣas, is aphrodisiac, benefits the eyes, and removes poison.

children.text: mandānalatvaṃ balahānimugrāṃ viṣṭambhatāṃ netrarujaṃ ca kuṣṭham
children.translated_text: But unprepared <s>mākṣika</s> mineral, being heavy, causes weak digestion, severe loss of strength, constipation, pain in the eyes, and skin disease,
and it also produces impurity, preceded by sores.

children.text: añjanaṃ mecakaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ sauvīraṃ ca suvīrajam
children.translated_text: <s>Añjana</s> is <s>mecaka</s>, black, <s>sauvīra</s>, and born in <s>Suvīra</s>.

children.text: kapotaṃ yāmuneyaṃ ca srotojaṃ sāritaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: It is <s>kapota</s>, <s>yāmuneya</s>, channel-born, and also <s>sārita</s>.
The wise declare <s>sauvīra</s> collyrium to be extremely cold.
It removes poison, hiccup disorders, eye disease, and poison.
<s>Samudraphena</s> is foam, dry or not dry, and born from the ocean.

children.text: vidyād udadhiphenaṃ ca proktaṃ sāgarajaṃ malam ||
children.translated_text: One should know it as ocean-foam, and it is called sea-born impurity.
<s>Samudraphena</s> is cooling and prevents suppuration of the ear.
It is scraping for eye diseases, cold, and destroys poison.
It benefits the eyes, removes bleeding disorders, and is remembered as removing abdominal tumors and spleen disease.

children.text: cakṣuṣyā dṛkprasādā ca saiva proktā kulatthikā
children.translated_text: The same is called <s>kulatthikā</s>, beneficial to the eyes and clarifying the sight.
<s>Kulālī</s>, beneficial to vision, is <s>kumbhakārī</s> and remover of impurity.

children.text: himā proktā kaṣāyā ca viṣaṃ sthāvarajaṅgamam
children.translated_text: It is said to be cooling and astringent; properly applied, it destroys poison, both stationary and moving.
It also destroys many discharges from the eyes.
And it removes the defects of eruptions, itching, eye-salve disorders, and wounds.
<s>Rasāñjana</s> is <s>tārkṣyaśaila</s>, born from rasa, and arising from rasa.
It is <s>rasagarbha</s>, best of rasas, and produced from a decoction of <s>dārvī</s>.
<s>Rasāñjana</s> is cold and bitter, and removes bleeding disorders, pitta, and phlegm.
It removes hiccup and asthma, improves complexion, and removes disease and poison.
<s>Puṣpāñjana</s> is <s>puṣpaketu</s>, floral, and flower-collyrium.
It is born of brass, brass-flower, brass-blossom, and floral.
<s>Puṣpāñjana</s> is cold and destroys hiccup that is extremely difficult to overcome.
It destroys the mass of eye diseases and renders poison non-poisonous.
<s>Śilājatu</s> is <s>atithi</s>, mountain-born, and born from rock.
It is <s>jatvaśmaja</s>, <s>aśmajatu</s>, said to be mineral-born and mountain-born.
<s>Śilājatu</s> is bitter, pungent, hot, and a rejuvenative.
It destroys urinary disease, insanity, stones, swelling, skin disease, and epilepsy.
It destroys wasting, swelling, abdominal disease, and piles, and conquers bladder pains.
<s>Gairika</s> is red mineral; copper-mineral is <s>gavedhuka</s>.
There is also stone-red ochre, and the second is golden-red ochre.
Stone-red ochre is said to be hard and copper-colored.

children.text: viśado gairikaḥ snigdhaḥ kaṣāyo madhuro himaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Gairika</s> is clear, unctuous, astringent, sweet, and cold.
It benefits the eyes, removes bleeding disorders, vomiting, hiccup, and poison.
Another is <s>suvarṇagairika</s>; from it they know red dust.
<s>Suvarṇagairika</s> is very red, unctuous, and smooth.

children.text: svādu snigdhaṃ himaṃ netryaṃ kaṣāyaṃ raktapittajit
children.translated_text: It is sweet, unctuous, cold, good for the eyes, astringent, and conquers bleeding disorders.
<s>Suvarṇagairika</s> removes hiccup, vomiting, and poison, and stops bleeding.

children.text: katakaṃ chedanīyaṃ ca kataṃ kataphalaṃ matam
children.translated_text: <s>Kataka</s> is <s>chedanīya</s>, <s>kata</s>, and is considered <s>kataphala</s>.
It is the water-clearing fruit, smooth, and conquers disorders of the eyes.
They say <s>kataka</s> is cooling and destroys thirst and poison.
When used properly as a collyrium, it destroys diseases arising in the eyes.

children.text: katakasya phalaṃ tiktaṃ cakṣuṣyaṃ śītalaṃ mṛdu
children.translated_text: The fruit of <s>kataka</s> is bitter, beneficial to the eyes, cooling, and mild.
It clears water and conquers painful gravel and stones.
<s>Lodhra</s> is <s>rodhra</s>, <s>śābaraka</s>, <s>tilvaka</s>, <s>tilaka</s>, and tree.
It is <s>tirīṭaka</s>, stemless, <s>bhillī</s>, and the <s>śambara</s> tree.
<s>Lodhra</s> is cold and astringent, and removes thirst and anorexia.
It is said to destroy poison; it is dry, absorbent, and removes phlegm.
<s>Kramuka</s> is <s>paṭṭikāroghna</s>, bark, and thick bark.
It is old-leaved, large-leaved, <s>paṭṭī</s>, and clarifier of lac.
The pair of <s>lodhra</s>s is astringent, cold, and conquers wind, phlegm, and blood disorders.
It benefits the eyes and removes poison; among them, bark-<s>lodhra</s> is superior.
<s>Śaṅkha</s> is water-born, conch, cloud-giver, and long-sounding.
It is sweet-voiced, long-resonant, white, and an ornament of <s>Śrī</s>.

children.text: śaṅkhaḥ svāduḥ kaṭuḥ pāke vīrye coṣṇaḥ prakīrtitaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Śaṅkha</s> is sweet, pungent in digestion, and proclaimed hot in potency.
It conquers indigestion and pain, benefits the eyes, and conquers bleeding disorders.
This group beginning with sandalwood is declared to be the third group.
It is fit for prosperous enjoyers and generally rests on the quality of fragrance.

children.text: suvarṇaṃ kanakaṃ rukmaṃ śātakumbhaṃ ca kāñcanam
children.translated_text: <s>Suvarṇa</s> is gold, <s>kanaka</s>, <s>rukma</s>, <s>śātakumbha</s>, and <s>kāñcana</s>.
<s>Jāmbūnada</s>, <s>jātarūpa</s>, <s>hiraṇya</s>, <s>hema</s>, and <s>hāṭaka</s> are names of gold.
<s>Cāmīkara</s>, beautiful jewel, <s>tapanīya</s>, and yellow are also its names.
It is remembered as <s>śrīketana</s>, fit for ornaments, and beautiful in form.

children.text: vīryaṃ vidhatte harate ca rogān karoti saukhyaṃ prabalendriyatvam
children.translated_text: Gold produces potency, removes diseases, and brings comfort and powerful senses.

children.text: śukrasya śuddhiṃ balavarṇavīryamojaśca puṣṭiṃ pradadāti hema ||
children.translated_text: Gold grants purity of semen, strength, complexion, vigor, <s>ojas</s>, and nourishment.

children.text: balaṃ ca vīryaṃ harate narāṇāṃ rogavrajān poṣayatīha kāye
children.translated_text: But defective gold takes away men's strength and vigor and nourishes hosts of diseases here in the body.

children.text: asaukhyadaṃ tacca sadaivamevaṃ rukmaṃ sadoṣaṃ maraṇaṃ karoti ||
children.translated_text: That faulty <s>rukma</s> always gives discomfort in this way and causes death.

children.text: raupyaṃ saudhaṃ sitaṃ tāraṃ rajataṃ taptarūpam
children.translated_text: Silver is <s>raupya</s>, <s>saudha</s>, white, <s>tāra</s>, <s>rajata</s>, and refined in form.

children.text: śubhraṃ kupyaṃ vasuśreṣṭhaṃ ruciraṃ śvetakaṃ matam ||
children.translated_text: It is considered bright, <s>kupya</s>, the best wealth, lovely, and whitish.
It is <s>candrahāsa</s>, moon-bodied, moon-splendor, and great wealth.
They call it <s>vākyala</s>, excellent, and also <s>raśmijāla</s>.

children.text: tāraṃ ca tārayati rogasamudrapāraṃ dehasya saukhyakaraṇaṃ palitaṃ valiṃ ca
children.translated_text: <s>Tāra</s> carries one across the ocean of disease, makes the body comfortable, and removes greying hair and wrinkles.

children.text: varṇyaṃ viṣaghnamamalaṃ harati prasahya vṛṣyaṃ punarnavakaraṃ kurute cirāyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: It improves complexion, destroys poison, forcefully removes impurity, is aphrodisiac, makes one renewed, and produces long life.

children.text: apakvatāraṃ prakaroti tāpaṃ viḍbandhanaṃ yacchati śukranāśam
children.translated_text: Uncooked silver produces fever, causes constipation, and destroys semen.
It is well known to cause lack of skill, loss of vigor and strength, and to nourish great diseases.
Copper is <s>tāmra</s>, <s>mlecchamukha</s>, <s>śulva</s>, red, and red metal.

children.text: udumbaraṃ tryambakaṃ ca vidyāttvāṣṭraṃ ca nāmataḥ ||
children.translated_text: One should know it by the names <s>udumbara</s>, <s>tryambaka</s>, and <s>tvāṣṭra</s>.

children.text: gulmaṃ ca kuṣṭhaṃ ca gudāmayaṃ ca śūlāni śophodarapāṇḍurogān
children.translated_text: Properly incinerated copper destroys abdominal tumors, skin disease, diseases of the anus, colics, swelling, abdominal enlargement, and anemia.
It also destroys nausea, piercing pain, dizziness, delusion, and burning.

children.text: śulvaṃ tanau nayati śeṣamaśeṣadhātūn rogān karoti vividhāṃśca nihanti kāntim
children.translated_text: Copper, if it leaves a residue in the body, carries it into all the tissues, creates various diseases, and destroys beauty.

children.text: kuṣṭhaṃ rujaṃ ca viṣamaṃ kurute viśeṣāt pākena hīnamiha vāntivirekakāri ||
children.translated_text: Especially when undercooked, it causes skin disease, pain, and irregular disorder here, and produces vomiting and purging.

children.text: hantyāyur uccaiḥ kurute'titāpaṃ mūrcchāṃ vidhatte harate ca śukram
children.translated_text: It greatly destroys life, produces excessive fever, causes fainting, and removes semen.

children.text: nānāgadānāṃ ca sahāyakartāśuddhaśca śulvo'tra ca jīvahartā ||
children.translated_text: Impure copper here assists many diseases and takes life.

children.text: trapu trapukamānīlaṃ raṅgaṃ vaṅgaṃ ca piccaṭam
children.translated_text: Tin is <s>trapu</s>, <s>trapuka</s>, <s>ānīla</s>, <s>raṅga</s>, <s>vaṅga</s>, and <s>piccaṭa</s>.
It is <s>guruśreṣṭha</s>, salty, <s>suraṭī</s>, <s>nīlikā</s>, and dense.
Tin is slightly bitter, hot, dry, and destructive of phlegm.
It pacifies aggravated pitta and conquers disorders born from worms.

children.text: pākena hīnau khalu nāgavaṅgau duṣṭāni gulmāni tathā vikoṣṭham
children.translated_text: Lead and tin, when undercooked, certainly produce malignant abdominal tumors and disorders of the bowel.
They also produce anemia, stupefaction, wasting, wind disorders, swelling, fistula, leucoderma, depigmentation, and skin disease.
They powerfully and constantly cause urinary disease, stones, abscesses, and other chief diseases, beginning with loss of strength.

children.text: viṣopamau raktavikāravṛndaṃ kṣayaṃ ca kṛcchrāṇi kaphajvaraṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: They are like poison and cause groups of blood disorders, wasting, difficult urinary conditions, and phlegmatic fever.

children.text: rītikā kākatuṇḍī ca dvividhaṃ pittalaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: <s>Rītikā</s> and <s>kākatuṇḍī</s>: brass is of two kinds.
<s>Rīti</s> is <s>lohaka</s>, tawny, <s>kapiloha</s>, and <s>suvarṇaka</s>.
It is <s>āra</s>, <s>saiṃhalaka</s>, harsh, and thorn-wood.
Royal <s>rīti</s> is remembered as queen, princess, and <s>maheśvarī</s>.
It is <s>brahmāṇī</s>, <s>brahmarīti</s>, tawny, and yellowish too.

children.text: rītidvayaṃ sakalapāṇḍusamīraṇaghnaṃ rūkṣaṃ saraṃ kṛmiharaṃ lavaṇaṃ viṣaghnam
children.translated_text: The two kinds of <s>rīti</s> destroy all anemia and wind; they are dry, mobile, worm-destroying, salty, and poison-destroying.

children.text: vṛṣyaṃ valīpalitanāśanam ugram āyurvṛddhiṃ karoti sahasā ca rasāyanāgryam ||
children.translated_text: They are aphrodisiac, remove wrinkles and grey hair, are powerful, increase life suddenly, and are foremost as a <s>rasāyana</s>.
Lead is <s>sīsaka</s>, <s>nāga</s>, serpent, black serpent, and snake.
It is favored by foreigners, distinguished, favored by yogins, and <s>cīrapiṣṭaka</s>.

children.text: nāgo hi nāgasamameva balaṃ dadāti vyādhīn vināśayati cāyuralaṃ karoti
children.translated_text: Lead indeed gives strength equal to that of an elephant, destroys diseases, and makes life abundant.

children.text: sadyo vivardhayati so'pi pradhānadhātuṃ mṛtyuṃ nivārayati cāpi bhujaṅgarājaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That king of serpents at once increases the chief tissue and also wards off death.

children.text: kāṃsyaṃ lohaṃ nijaṃ ghoṣaṃ prakāśaṃ kāṃsyakaṃ balam
children.translated_text: Bronze is <s>kāṃsya</s>, metal, its own resonance, brightness, <s>kāṃsyaka</s>, and strength.
It has been taught with synonymous words such as <s>ghoṣapuṣpa</s>.

children.text: kāṃsyaṃ tiktoṣṇarūkṣaṃ ca laghu lekhi prakīrtitam
children.translated_text: Bronze is declared bitter, hot, dry, light, and scraping.
When used in collyrium and similar preparations, it bestows divine sight.

children.text: lohaṃ śastraṃ ghanaṃ piṇḍaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ pāraśavaṃ śivam
children.translated_text: Iron is <s>loha</s>, weapon, solid mass, sharp, <s>pāraśava</s>, and auspicious.
It is <s>ayaḥ</s>, black iron, heroic, bee-like, and black metal.

children.text: muṇḍaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ ca kāntaṃ ca triprakāramayaḥ smṛtam
children.translated_text: Iron is remembered as of three kinds: <s>muṇḍa</s>, sharp, and magnetic.

children.text: mṛdu kaṇṭaṃ kaḍāraṃ ca trividhaṃ muṇḍamucyate ||
children.translated_text: <s>Muṇḍa</s> is said to be threefold: soft, <s>kaṇṭa</s>, and <s>kaḍāra</s>.

children.text: kharasāraṃ ca hartālaṃ tālaṃ ballaṃ ca vajjaram
children.translated_text: <s>Kharasāra</s>, orpiment, <s>tāla</s>, <s>balla</s>, and <s>vajjara</s>,
together with that called black iron, are said to be the six kinds of sharp iron.
<s>Bhrāmara</s>, magnet, <s>rañjaka</s>, and <s>ālocaka</s>,

children.text: evaṃ caturvidhaṃ kāntaṃ romakāntaṃ ca pañcamam ||
children.translated_text: thus magnetic iron is fourfold; <s>romakānta</s> is the fifth.
Iron is astringent and conquers swelling, colic, piles, skin disease, anemia, and urinary disorder.
Iron is bitter, hot, and dry; it is supreme for removing anemia.
It removes phlegm and pitta in men and is an unsurpassed <s>rasāyana</s>.

children.text: doṣakāri gadakāri cāyasaṃ cedaśuddham asusaṃskṛtaṃ dhruvam
children.translated_text: Iron certainly causes doṣas and diseases if it is impure and improperly processed.

children.text: pāṭavaṃ na tanute śarīrake dāruṇāṃ hṛdi rujaṃ karoti ca ||
children.translated_text: It does not produce bodily competence and causes terrible pain in the heart.
<s>Vartaloha</s>, <s>vaṭṭaloha</s>, <s>vartaka</s>, and simply metal are its names.

children.text: vartulohaṃ ca vikhyātaṃ pañcalohaṃ ca nīlikā ||
children.translated_text: It is famous as <s>vartuloha</s>, <s>pañcaloha</s>, and <s>nīlikā</s>.
One should know <s>vartaloha</s> as cooling, sour, and pungent.
It is dry, removes phlegmatic disorders, and destroys pains arising from pitta.

children.text: lohocchiṣṭaṃ ca maṇḍūraṃ kiṭṭaṃ caiva malodbhavam
children.translated_text: Iron dross is <s>maṇḍūra</s>, slag, and that which arises from waste.
It is said to be born from iron, the exudation of iron, and the remnant of iron.
It is excellent for removing <s>āmavāta</s> and is foremost in destroying anemia, urinary disorder, and disease.
It conquers severe skin disease, wind, bleeding disorder, and vāta disorder, and destroys wrinkles produced by old age.
<s>Pārada</s> is also <s>rudraretas</s>, <s>rasaloha</s>, and <s>mahārasa</s>.
It is <s>rasendra</s>, <s>capala</s>, <s>sūta</s>, <s>pāradīya</s>, and the best of rasas.
<s>Pārada</s> destroys worms and skin disease, promotes life, and is an excellent giver of sight.
It greatly strengthens, is somewhat astringent, and, when stupefied or processed, removes disease.

children.text: saṃskārahīnaṃ khalu sūtarājaṃ seveta yastasya karoti bādhām
children.translated_text: But one who uses the king of <s>sūta</s> without purification is afflicted by it.
It surely brings about destruction of the body and produces skin disease and other disorders in people.
<s>Hiṅgula</s> is <s>darada</s>, <s>mleccha</s>, <s>hiṅgūla</s>, and powdered mercury.
Another name is <s>maṇirāgakara</s>, and by name it is that which colors the skin.

children.text: hiṅgulaṃ kaṭukaṃ pāke vīrye coṣṇaṃ prakīrtitam
children.translated_text: <s>Hiṅgula</s> is declared to be pungent in digestion and hot in potency.
It is remembered as breaking down poison, skin disease, erysipelas, and other skin disorders.
<s>Hiṅgula</s> is sweet, bitter, hot, and removes wind and phlegm.
When used, it removes fever arising from all three doṣas and from paired doṣas.
<s>Vaikrānta</s> is known as <s>krānta</s>; it is also <s>vajra</s> and earth-dust.
It is <s>gonasa</s>, small thunderbolt, and aged diamond; but <s>vajraka</s> is another name.
It is said to be of seven kinds and to perform many actions.
The best <s>vaikrānta</s> is six-angled, sharp-edged, clear, and colored like a rainbow.

children.text: taduttamaṃ tu vaikrāntaṃ hitaṃ proktaṃ rasāyane
children.translated_text: That excellent <s>vaikrānta</s> is said to be beneficial in rejuvenation therapy.
It conquers urinary disorder, impotence, premature old age, wasting disease, <s>grahaṇī</s>, and cough.
<s>Vaikrānta</s> is aphrodisiac, rejuvenating, strengthening, and kindles the digestive fire.
<s>Vaikrāntaka</s> grants life, produces strength and complexion, is highly aphrodisiac, gives understanding, and removes the whole mass of doṣas.
It kindles bright digestion, has qualities equal to the thunderbolt, is swift-acting, and indeed makes the body strong and iron-like.
Unpurified diamond is heavy and causes anemia, burning, pain in the side, loss of appetite, and skin disease.

children.text: śuddhaṃ mṛtaṃ saukhyabalapradaṃ syād vaikrāntabhasmāpi rasāyanaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: When purified and calcined it gives comfort and strength, and the ash of <s>vaikrānta</s> too is rejuvenating.
<s>Gārutmata</s> is <s>marakata</s>, <s>rauhiṇeya</s>, and the green gem.
It is <s>sauparṇa</s>, vomited by <s>Garuḍa</s>, the gem of the wise, and born from stone.
It is enemy of poison, <s>vāyavāla</s>, <s>gāruḍa</s>, and comparable to <s>Rudra</s>.

children.text: rauhiṇeyaṃ viṣaghnaṃ ca śītalaṃ madhuraṃ rase ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rauhiṇeya</s> destroys poison, is cooling, and is sweet in taste.
It removes acid dyspepsia, is aphrodisiac, gives nourishment, and destroys spirits.
<s>Hīraka</s> is <s>bhidura</s>, <s>vajra</s>, excellent gem, thunderbolt, and <s>pavi</s>.

children.text: sūcivaktraṃ varāhaṃ ca kuliśaṃ bhārgavaṃ smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: It is remembered as needle-mouthed, boar, thunderbolt, and <s>bhārgava</s>.
The unbreakable, veinless, firm gem is remembered as <s>bhārgavaka</s>.
It is six-angled, many-edged, and born from earth beneath the ocean for a hundred crores of years.

children.text: rujāṃ samūhaṃ harate narāṇāṃ balaṃ surūpaṃ vidadhāti yuktyā
children.translated_text: Used properly, it removes the mass of people's pains and produces strength and beauty.

children.text: dehasya saukhyaṃ ca sadā karoti ciraṃ tathāyuḥ palitaṃ ca hanti ||
children.translated_text: It always brings comfort to the body, prolongs life, and removes gray hair.

children.text: āyuṣpradaṃ jhaṭiti sadguṇadaṃ ca vṛṣyaṃ doṣatrayapraśamanaṃ sakalāmayaghnam
children.translated_text: Diamond grants life, quickly gives good qualities, is aphrodisiac, pacifies the three doṣas, and destroys all diseases.
It produces the good qualities of binding and killing lord mercury, is a lamp, a conqueror of death, and truly like nectar.

children.text: pīḍāṃ vidhatte vividhāṃ narāṇāṃ kuṣṭhaṃ kṣayaṃ pāṇḍugadaṃ ca duṣṭam
children.translated_text: Unpurified diamond causes various pains in people, skin disease, wasting disease, and severe anemia.
It causes very difficult pain in the heart and side, and, being heavy, produces burning.

children.text: rājāvartaśca rājā ca nīlāśmā tu nṛpopalaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Rājāvarta</s> is <s>rājā</s>; blue stone is <s>nṛpopala</s>.
It is gold-ore, <s>rājādri</s>, and also <s>rājaprastara</s>.
<s>Rājāvarta</s> is pungent, unctuous, cooling, and destroys pitta.
When used in ornaments, it brings good fortune to people.
<s>Mauktika</s> is shell-born, blister-shell-born, and produced from a shell.
It is most worthy of ornament, excellent, <s>śauktika</s>, and also <s>bhautika</s>.

children.text: mauktikaṃ madhuraṃ śītaṃ saraṃ dṛṣṭibhavaṃ gadam
children.translated_text: <s>Mauktika</s> is sweet, cooling, flowing, and uproots disease arising in the eyes.
It also uproots pitta; by contact with a necklace it removes burning.
<s>Pravāla</s> is <s>vidruma</s>, red, fit for ornament, and born from a fine creeper.
It is sea-born, very red, and produced from a stone-creeper.
Coral having the luster of ripe bimbī fruit, round or long, and not crooked,
unctuous, without wounds, and large is auspicious in these seven ways.
But coral that is pale, gray, dry, wounded, full of fissures,

children.text: nirbhāraṃ śubhravarṇaṃ ca neṣyate saptadhā tvidam ||
children.translated_text: light in weight, and white in color is not desired in these seven ways.
<s>Pravālaka</s> is flowing, cooling, and removes phlegm, pitta, and other doṣas.
It is desired for counteracting disorders of the eyes and for destroying poison.
